    Item text is the English SHAI-18 original, but the study administered a Spanish translation whose wording the paper never quotes. The 14/4 split between the two subscales is confirmed against the paper's subscale statistics, but item order *within* each subscale rests on `HAnx<N>` being the instrument's item *N*

- table: abdullah_2024_bsq_sev24
  issue: |-
    Item text is the English half of a bilingual instrument table, but the study administered the Malay BSQ-M. The source the study cites for its instrument (Mahd-Abdullah et al. 2021, IJERPH 18:2487, CC BY) lists every item in both languages against the same codes, so the administered Malay wording does exist and is not what ships here; `language` records the administration as Malay. `option_text` is empty because the BSQ's response options are per-item multiple-choice categories that neither paper publishes. `SEV241` is marked a reverse-scored item in the source

  issue: |-
    The paper describes originality as coded on a 0-4 scale, but the IRW table (and `option_text`) is on 1-5. This is not a shift introduced here: the authors' own deposited file ([osf.io/qcmex](https://osf.io/qcmex/files/u3yv4)) already codes `rater1`-`rater4` as 1-5, and the processing script does no recoding, so the table reproduces the source faithfully. The discrepancy is between the paper's text and the authors' shared data; read the 1-5 values as the paper's 0-4 categories shifted by one
- table: 16_personalityfactors
  issue: |-
    The source's own instructions describe the scale as "(1) disagree ... (5) agree" while its per-item codebook labels it "strongly disagree ... strongly agree"; `option_text` follows the codebook. Item `163` is the one column the codebook omits, so its text comes from the IPIP scale listing rather than the dataset's own documentation
- table: almuqbil_2022_epds
  issue: |-
    Participants completed the Arabic EPDS translation (Ghubash et al. 1997); the item text here is the English wording used to label the items in the study's own data file, so it is not what respondents read
- table: alkouri_2025_icu_stressors
  issue: |-
    The source questionnaire changes the wording of its second response option partway through the scale -- items 01-14 offer "Barely" and items 15-29 offer "Rarely" for the same value 2 -- so option text varies by item; transcribed as the source gives it
- table: alsuhibani_2022_loc
  issue: |-
    The paper's Methods describes this as a five-point scale, but the live data and the study's own SPSS file both show a genuine 6-point "Strongly disagree" ... "Strongly agree" scale; the data file was followed rather than the paper text
- table: alves_2017_hamd17
  issue: |-
    Item text follows a canonical reproduction of Hamilton's original (1960) HDRS-17, which scores item 9 (Agitation) 0-2, but this study's data scores it 0-4 -- so `HamD9Baixa` responses of 3 and 4 have no option label. Item text is also a canonical reproduction rather than the study's own materials, and item-to-text alignment follows the instrument's standard order rather than an explicit map
- table: amarilla_2020_lawton_brody
  issue: |-
    `resp` (0/1) is the Lawton-Brody dependency score rather than the administered response: each domain offers 3-5 instrument levels that collapse to able/unable, so `option_text` names the scored category and lists the levels sharing it instead of a single literal option label. The study's data supplement also records only the total IADL score, so the item-to-domain mapping follows the standard Lawton & Brody (1969) ordering rather than an explicit map, and item text comes from the canonical instrument
- table: american_multiracial_face
  issue: |-
    Each item is one photograph rated on one attribute, and the `item` codes are arbitrary integers assigned when the study's 19 separate rating files were stacked -- they carry no meaning and must not be read as an item order. `item_text` is therefore a constructed description of the stimulus rather than transcribed text; the verbatim rating question is the `section_prompt`. The AMFD PhotoID named in `item_text` is not stated in the source materials and was recovered by matching per-face rating means against the published norming table, and 9 faces (171 items) were never released in the AMFD and so carry no PhotoID. Only scale points 1 and 7 were labelled in the original survey, so `option_text` is blank for 2-6. Separately, the table has no Black-prototypicality ratings for the smiling photographs: the source repository provides them, but the IRW processing script does not read that file
- table: an_2020_efl_self_regulated
  issue: |-
    The table name signals one instrument but the table pools three administered in the same survey: the TSELSS strategy items (Q1-Q26), an English-learning enjoyment/environment block (Q27-Q33), and a 16-item English language self-efficacy questionnaire (Q34-Q49). Item text is the original Chinese from the study's own data file. Only the two endpoints of the 7-point scale are labelled in that file, so `option_text` is blank for values 2-6
- table: anjum_2022_gad7
  issue: |-
    The IRW table covers 6 of the GAD-7's 7 items: item 1 ("Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge") is present in the study's data file but was not included in the IRW release. Two item wordings and the response anchors follow that file's own labels, which differ from canonical GAD-7 wording -- "not being able to sleep or control worrying" for "stop or control", "hart to sit still" for "hard", and "More than half of the days" for "More than half the days". The instructions are the canonical GAD-7 stem; the data file carries none
- table: AOMT_BR_SF_EDPANAB_Geiger_2021_AOT
  issue: |-
    The table carries 14 item codes for a 10-item scale. AOT3_rev, AOT5_rev, AOT7_rev and AOT8_rev are reverse-coded duplicates of AOT3, AOT5, AOT7 and AOT8 rather than additional items -- the same statement, with the response options in reverse order -- so they carry their parent item's text and reversed `option_text`
- table: AOMT_BR_SF_EDPANAB_Geiger_2021_BRS
  issue: |-
    The table name signals the Bullshit Receptivity Scale alone, but it combines that scale's 10 items (BSR\*) with the 10 motivational-quotation control statements (MOT\*) from the same study; both blocks were rated on the same "profoundness" scale
- table: arnulf_2022_general_knowledge
  issue: |-
    The general-knowledge test was open-answer, so participants did not choose from the options shown here: `option_text` gives the Correct/Incorrect scoring labels the study's data file attaches to 0 and 1. Item text is verbatim from that file, including its "principle street for finance in New York" where the paper's prose reads "principal"
- table: arora2025_blueq_synchronous
  issue: |-
    The study's data file records only numeric codes, so the response anchors and the section prompt are taken from the published BLUE-Q instrument. That instrument's prompt describes a "face-to-face component", while this study administered the synchronous sessions as online workshops -- the item text itself, which is verbatim from the study's own spreadsheet, refers to "face-to-face online workshops"
- table: art
  issue: |-
    The Author Recognition Test presents a checklist of names with no printed response labels, so `option_text` ("Checked"/"Not checked") describes the check-box rather than quoting the instrument, and `item_text` repeats the author name shown on the checklist. Only the 50 real-author items are in the IRW table; the 50 foils were dropped upstream. The name "T.S. Elliot" is kept as the source data spells it (canonically "T. S. Eliot")
- table: artistic_preferences
  issue: |-
    The table name describes only the first of three instruments administered in the same session: items 1-30 are the Artistic Preferences Scales, items 31-40 the Ten Item Personality Inventory, and items 41-56 a 16-word vocabulary check list. Items 1-30 have no text stem at all -- each is a pair of paintings, shown as images, that the respondent chooses between and rates the strength of the preference; the images are distributed with the source dataset. Only the two extreme points of that 1-5 scale carry anchors, so `option_text` is blank for 2-4
- table: arzamoncunill_2023_epq_clinical
  issue: |-
    Ten of the 22 items here are not the wording respondents read. The study ran a 43-item pretest pool but published full item wording, in Spanish, only for the 26 items kept in its final questionnaire, while this table holds all 22 clinical-care items of the pretest pool. The 12 that survived carry their administered Spanish from Appendix S3; the other 10 have no published wording in any language, so they keep the short category descriptor the study's supplement gives for each item number ("Editable agenda", "Videoconference"), which names what the item is about rather than quoting it. Those 10 are identifiable by an empty `item_text_translated`. Two of the 12 English translations are the authors' own, printed in both languages in Appendix S1; the other 10 were produced by IRW rather than by the study. The 7-point anchors are published in English only ("very much disagree", "very much agree"), so `option_text` is English throughout. The study's own data file carries no variable or value labels; the item numbers are matched exactly, and the 12 Spanish items are tied to their codes through the supplement's number-to-descriptor map, cross-checked against the retained-item list in the study's factor analyses
- table: audretsch_2021_entrepreneurial_ecosystems
  issue: |-
    Item text is the untruncated form of the study data file's variable labels, recovered from its Stata do-file because the `.dta` labels are cut off at Stata's 80-character cap. For the `ee_quality` item the paper's own section 4.2 quotes a different wording ("There is a strong focus on growth-oriented and productive entrepreneurship activity in my region (city)") from the data-file label that is shipped here ("There is a strong entrepreneurship ecosystem (EE) in my region (city)"). Several labels are ungrammatical or unclosed in the source and are transcribed as they stand. Only the endpoints of the 1-7 scale (1 = very weak, 7 = very strong) are documented, so the intermediate options are blank
- table: autonomysupport_mokken
  issue: |-
    The item "Decide" is reverse-worded in the original questionnaire, but the responses in this table are the raw, unreversed scores, so the same anchors apply to it as to every other item. Item text is the English rendering the `mokken` package documents for a questionnaire administered in Dutch. Only the two extreme anchors are documented (1 = not at all/never, 5 = certainly/always)
- table: avilesgonzalez2019_ces
  issue: |-
    Item text comes from the study's SPSS file, which stores the English Caring Efficacy Scale wording even though the respondents were Italian nurses, so it is not what they read. Several typographical errors in those labels are preserved here as the source has them -- one item is missing its opening "If", another reads "Ioften", and several begin with a lowercase "i"
- table: baaziz_2023_sms2
  issue: |-
    The text shown for item 16 is probably not the item respondents answered, and should not be used as the wording of that item. The paper prints "So that others praise me for what I do" at position 16, which is external-regulation content, but in the data item 16 behaves as amotivation: it correlates 0.88-0.90 with items 17 and 18, the other two amotivation items, and essentially zero (0.02, 0.04, -0.03) with the three external-regulation items 13-15. Position 16 in the SMS-II is an amotivation item, so the paper's table appears to misprint its wording. The misprint is in both languages -- the Arabic printed at position 16 carries the same external-regulation content -- and both are shipped unchanged rather than substituted with a guess. `item_text` is the administered Arabic from the paper's Table 7, with the authors' own English back-translation in `item_text_translated`. The 7-point scale anchors are an exception: the paper gives them only in English ("Not at all true", "Very true"), so `option_text` holds English rather than what respondents read, and its `_translated` twin is empty. Only the endpoints are documented, so options 2-6 are blank
- table: baka2023_jcs
  issue: |-
    Item stems are in Polish as administered, but the response anchors carried by the study's data file are English glosses rather than the Polish wording participants saw
- table: baka2023_olbi
  issue: |-
    Only 8 of the published OLBI's 16 items are present in the study's data file, and those 8 are what this table covers. Item stems are in Polish as administered, but the response anchors carried by the data file are English glosses rather than the Polish wording participants saw
- table: baka2023_uwes
  issue: |-
    Item stems are in Polish as administered, but the response anchors carried by the study's data file are English glosses rather than the Polish wording participants saw
- table: bakker_2020_rses
  issue: |-
    The item codes for this table must not be read as item content. Seven of the ten columns in the study's SPSS file carry a variable label that contradicts the column name, and the data show the labels are the reliable half: the column named `goodqualities303` is labelled "All in all, I am inclined to feel that I am a failure" and averages 1.47 on a 1-4 Strongly Disagree..Strongly Agree scale, while `nogood302` is labelled "I feel that I have a number of good qualities" and averages 3.27. Every negatively-worded label sits at the floor and every positively-worded one at the ceiling, which a positively-worded self-esteem item could not do in a general sample. Read in column order the labels reproduce a standard circulated administration order of the scale, so the names appear to have been assigned by numbering the columns in Rosenberg's original order without noticing the form was permuted. The text shipped here follows the labels; join on the item code and read the text, not the code. Responses are stored raw and unreversed. Note also that the paper's Methods states the scale ran 1 = strongly agree to 4 = strongly disagree, the reverse of the data file's own value labels; the data follow the file
- table: bang_2023_self_esteem
  issue: |-
    The item order in this table was reconstructed, not read from any key, and the item text is not what respondents saw. Neither the study's data file (bare codes S1-S10) nor the paper ties any code to an item, so the shipped text is the canonical English Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale wording placed in an order inferred from the reverse-keying pattern in the raw responses; the study administered the Korean version (Jon, 1974), whose wording is not reproduced anywhere. What the data establish is each item's polarity: S1, S2, S4, S6 and S7 intercorrelate positively (+0.31 to +0.73) and S3, S5, S9 and S10 form the opposing block, which rules out the scale's original item numbering, and S8 is identifiable by its distinctive near-zero correlation with the positive block. What they do not establish is the order within each polarity block, so a swap between two same-polarity items -- S1 and S2, say -- is not excluded
- table: bartoli_2022_badge_notifications
  issue: |-
    This table records a single-click behavioural task rather than a questionnaire. Each participant saw one home screen of 15 app icons with a badge notification on one app and made a single click, so `resp` = 100 marks the one app that participant clicked first and 0 the other fourteen. The response-option text is descriptive; the task offered no labelled options. The item text gives each app's conventional name, with the Italian default-app labels left as administered
- table: beck_2021_iesr
  issue: |-
    `resp` values 1-4 are category indices, not scores. The study used the German IES-R (Maercker & Schuetzwohl, 1998), whose four anchors are ueberhaupt nicht / selten / manchmal / oft and whose traditional scoring weights that version prints are 0, 1, 3 and 5 -- so summing `resp` gives a different scale from the published one. Item text is that German form verbatim, including its pre-1996 orthography
- table: bitew_2020_lte
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own abbreviated SPSS variable labels ("self illness", "family death"), not the administered wording, which was in Amharic and was never published. Canonical Life Events Questionnaire wording was deliberately not substituted because this version departs from it: items 8-11 are reordered relative to the original sequence, and item 12 (intimate partner violence) is not an LTE-Q item at all
- table: bitew_2020_osss3
  issue: |-
    Item wording is the canonical English OSSS-3 rather than the study's administered Amharic version. One caveat on the mapping: item 1's variable label in the source file reads "others worry for me", which does not obviously correspond to the canonical item-1 content about how many people you can count on. It is identified as item 1 by its response structure instead -- it is the only one of the three offering four categories rather than five, which is the instrument's own signature, and the file's total column equals the sum of the three items for every case
- table: bitew_2020_phq9
  issue: |-
    Item wording is the canonical English PHQ-9; the study administered a locally validated Amharic translation whose exact wording is not published. The mapping to those canonical items is confirmed by the source file's own numbered symptom labels and by the paper's reported per-item means
- table: bitew_2020_self_efficacy
  issue: |-
    This table holds 9 of the General Self-Efficacy Scale's 10 items, and **its item codes are offset by one**: `SEFFICAn` is GSE item n+1, so `SEFFICA1` is GSE item 2. The source file does contain GSE item 1, under a differently-named column, but it was not shipped to the IRW. The response anchors are the authors' own shorthand for the GSE's Not at all true...Exactly true scale
- table: brederecke_2020_sis
  issue: |-
    Items 4 and 9 are stored reverse-coded in the source data, and the option text here follows that stored direction: for those two items `resp` = 1 is "strongly agree" and 5 is "strongly disagree", while the other nine run 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree. This is stated by the study's own file, which names those two columns "SIS Item 4 recoded" and "SIS Item 9 recoded" -- they are the scale's two negatively-worded items. `item_text` is the administered German from the paper's Table 3, which is headed "Original item (German version)", with the paper's English in `item_text_translated`. The five-point anchors are an exception: neither the paper nor the study's data file gives them in German -- the file labels its values "1" to "5" with no anchor text -- so `option_text` holds the English wording quoted above rather than what respondents read, and its `_translated` twin is empty
- table: broadband_inventories
  issue: |-
    The instructions, quoted verbatim from the test's own page, describe a five-point scale, but the items were administered on the seven-point Strongly disagree..Strongly agree scale that `resp` 1-7 encodes. The item wording is otherwise verbatim from the source codebook, including its typos (item 18 reads "when Im feeling badly")
- table: buczel_2022_inoculation_belief
  issue: |-
    Each of these six items covers six different question wordings. The study counterbalanced six scenarios across participants, so the sentence any one participant read depends on which scenario they saw; `item_text` therefore names the item's condition and quotes one scenario's wording as an example rather than presenting one participant's version as the item. Note also that the response scale displayed to participants ran 0-10 while `resp` is stored as 1-11, so the option text carries the displayed number and is deliberately not equal to `resp`
- table: bukurov_2022_sf36
  issue: |-
    Item and option wording is the public-domain English RAND 36-Item Health Survey. The study administered a Serbian-language SF-36, so this is canonical text rather than what participants read. The mapping to those canonical items is firm: the source file labels every column with its item, and the per-item response formats match the instrument's mixed structure exactly (5 levels for items 1, 2, 20, 22 and 32-36; 3 for items 3-12; 2 for 13-19; 6 for 21 and 23-31)
- table: busch_2022_course_alleviate
  issue: |-
    These are the checkbox options of a single select-all-that-apply survey question, not independently administered items: `resp` = 1 means the respondent ticked that aspect and 0 means they did not, so a 0 records the absence of a tick rather than substantive disagreement. The question was shown only to the respondents who reported depression symptoms while taking online science courses
- table: brederecke_2020_phq4
  issue: |-
    The item text is the study data file's own terse English variable labels ("little interest or pleasure in your activities"), which are neither the German wording the instrument was administered in nor the canonical PHQ-4 phrasing. The response options are that file's English labels too, and they likewise differ from the published PHQ-4 anchors -- "On single days" where the instrument reads "Several days". The `instructions` line is the canonical PHQ-4 stem, which the data file does not carry
- table: burgess_2025_soas
  issue: |-
    The item codes are non-contiguous -- SOAS5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12 -- because they refer to positions in the 13-item version administered in this study, of which these six were retained in the final scale. The study's data file carries no variable or value labels, so the item text and that numbering come from the paper's own item table rather than from the data. In this study the items were read aloud to children who were shown a fixed object, so the published instrument's opening line asking the respondent to choose and write down an object did not apply and is not included here
- table: brain_hemisphere
  issue: |-
    The `instructions` field describes the response scale rather than quoting an instruction shown to participants; the source dataset documents the scale but publishes no participant-facing instruction text. Only three of the five scale points were labelled (1 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 5 = Agree), so the option text is blank at 2 and 4. Note also that this 2015-16 dataset is the 20-item version of the scale; the version currently offered online has 24 items
- table: busch_2023_stigma
  issue: |-
    Despite the table name, these items are not stigma ratings. They are the participants' own binary self-reports of concealable identities -- LGBQ+, depression, anxiety, low SES, first-generation status, academic struggle, disability, community-college transfer -- while the study's actual 4-point perceived-stigma measure is not in the IRW table at all. Six of the eight items share the identical stem "I most closely identify as", so the item content lives entirely in the response options. For two items the binary 0 collapses several source options (for example mid and upper income both map to 0), and the option text joins those source options verbatim; "Decline to state" responses are dropped rather than coded
- table: butt_2022_cognitive_absorption
  issue: |-
    The study's data file contains four of the six Cognitive Absorption items -- CA3 and CA5 were dropped by the authors -- and it carries no variable labels for them, so the wording here comes from the appendix questionnaire, which lists the six items in order without codes. The alignment is therefore by position within that block
- table: butt_2022_institutional_factors
  issue: |-
    Eleven of the appendix's thirteen Institutional Factors items are in the data; IF3 and IF11 are absent from the study's own file and are not shipped. The data file gives no variable labels for these columns, so the wording comes from the appendix questionnaire by position within the block. One source typo was corrected: the appendix prints "students 'questions" with a misplaced opening quote, shipped here as "students' questions"
- table: butt_2022_actual_usage
  issue: |-
    This two-item scale does not use the questionnaire's 1-7 agreement scale: each item has its own response anchors -- a frequency scale for one and hours per week for the other -- so `instructions` is blank because the block's shared instruction does not apply
- table: buzgova_2023_rses
  issue: |-
    The item numbering here is an assumption that could not be independently confirmed. The study's data file carries no variable or value labels of any kind and the paper reproduces no items, so the text is the canonical English Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale mapped on the basis that RSES*n* is Rosenberg item *n*. That assumption is known to fail for this instrument: in `bakker_2020_rses` the columns were numbered in canonical order while the administered form was permuted. Here the responses are stored already reverse-scored -- every inter-item correlation is positive -- so the keying-polarity check that caught the other case cannot be run. One position does have positive support: RSES8 has both the lowest mean and the lowest item-rest correlation, the known signature of Rosenberg item 8 ("I wish I could have more respect for myself"). Positions 1-7, 9 and 10 rest on the numbering alone. The scale is also stored pre-reversed, so the same anchors apply to every item
- table: buzgova_2023_soc
  issue: |-
    Item text is the canonical English SOC-13; the study was Czech and its translation is not published in the paper or the data file, which carries no labels of any kind. The responses are stored already reverse-scored, so the option text for the five reverse-worded items (1, 2, 3, 7 and 10) is **flipped relative to the printed instrument**. Note also a discrepancy with the paper: it reports Cronbach's alpha of 0.92 for this scale, while the released data give 0.765 with corrected item-total correlations of 0.29-0.53
- table: buzgova_2023_gai
  issue: |-
    Item text is the canonical English Geriatric Anxiety Inventory; the study was Czech and its translation is not published, and the data file carries no labels of any kind. The mapping of code to item is supported but not settled: the instrument's published three-factor structure reproduces for 15 of the 20 items, with the three purely somatic items all behaving as expected, while five cognitive-versus-arousal items are ambiguous
- table: buzgova_2023_gds
  issue: |-
    Item text is the canonical English GDS-15; the study was Czech and its translation is not published in the paper or the data file, which carries no labels of any kind. The responses are stored already scored rather than raw, so `resp` = 1 always marks the depression-consistent answer and the option text follows that stored direction rather than the yes/no order printed on the questionnaire
- table: buzgova_2023_lsita
  issue: |-
    This table is the 12-item short form of the LSITA, and the item text is the canonical English wording -- the study was Czech and its translation is published nowhere accessible, the data file carries no labels, and the companion validation paper is paywalled. Items 2, 4, 5 and 6 are stored already reversed, so their option text is flipped relative to the printed instrument; the raw column sum reproduces the paper's published total exactly, which is what establishes that
- table: cacciatore_2021_crisis_care_satisfaction
  issue: |-
    The `resp` values are not the survey's own choice numbering. The questionnaire numbered its options 1 = Extremely satisfied down to 6 = N/A, while the IRW values are the processing script's recoding into ascending satisfaction, and the "N/A" responses are dropped rather than kept as a level. Item text is the matrix row label and the shared stem is recorded once in `instructions`; respondents rated only the care providers they actually encountered, which is why the number of responses varies widely across items
- table: chen_2022_sasc
  issue: |-
    Despite the table name, SASC here is the Smartphone Addiction Scale for College Students (SAS-C; Su et al., 2014), measuring problematic smartphone use -- **not** the Social Anxiety Scale for Children. The survey was administered in Chinese and the wording shown is the depositors' own English item labels from the SPSS file, as no Chinese original is published with the dataset
- table: criticalperiod_syntax
  issue: |-
    Six of the 95 items (q1, q2, q3, q5, q6 and q7) are sentence-to-picture matching items whose two answer choices are pictures. The source publishes those pictures only as figures, never as text, so **the `option_text` on those twelve rows is a machine-generated description of each picture rather than source wording** -- every one is prefixed `[machine-generated image description]` to make that unmistakable, and it is the only text in this table not transcribed from the source. Which picture belongs to which response is not guessed: the study's supplement prints an answer key naming the correct panel for each of the six, and because these are two-alternative forced choices, `resp` = 1 means the respondent chose that panel and `resp` = 0 means they chose the other. The remaining 89 items are grammaticality judgments and carry no `option_text` at all -- there `resp` is scored accuracy on a "choose all that apply" question, so no single option was chosen and any label would be invented. Separately, Question 10's four response options are printed in the supplement under a duplicated "c." label (a, b, c, c, with no "d."), so item q10_4 is identified as the fourth printed option, "What old are you?", by its position and by the answer key's grammaticality value; "How old are you?" (option 3) is grammatical in every dialect and is not in the table
- table: depression_anxiety_stress
  issue: |-
    This table pools three instruments administered in one openpsychometrics session, not the DASS alone: items 1-42 are the DASS-42, items 43-52 are the Ten Item Personality Inventory, and items 53-68 are a 16-word vocabulary checklist scored 0/1 (VCL6 "cuivocal", VCL9 "florted" and VCL12 "verdid" are not real words and were included as a validity check). The item codes are bare integers assigned by the processing script and carry no content of their own
- table: ftna_kasper_2022
  issue: |-
    The "items" in this table are whole-subject examination grades (Mathematics, Kiswahili and so on), not individual exam questions. Note also that the three core subjects **reuse one item code across both waves**, even though wave 0 is the primary-school PSLE and wave 1 the secondary-school FTNA -- so the same code refers to a different examination in each wave
- table: geography
  issue: |-
    Each item is a place on an outline map rather than a questionnaire item, and its `item_text` is the place name from the source archive's own lookup table **with the place type appended in parentheses -- an annotation added here, not part of the source name** -- because 46 place names are shared by two different places. The task presented no fixed answer options, so `option_text` labels the 0/1 correctness score rather than transcribing anything the learner saw
- table: riasec
  issue: |-
    Only items 1-48 of this table are the RIASEC interest inventory the table is named for. Items 49-58 are the Ten Item Personality Inventory and items 59-74 a 16-word vocabulary checklist, administered in the same session, and the three use different response scales (1-5, 1-7 and 0/1 respectively)
- table: sapa_personality
  issue: |-
    **17 of the 696 items ship the SAPA item dictionary's abbreviated shorthand -- bracketed or elided text -- rather than the full sentence the participant read**; the remaining 679 carry the full wording. Item text and the six response anchors both come from the SAPA-Project data release's own item dictionary (ItemInfo696) and code book
- table: emidy2024_fevs
  issue: |-
    The `.dta` this table is built from carries Stata variable labels truncated at 80 characters, so **the item wording shipped here is OPM's own published 2022 FEVS instrument text (Appendix B of the 2022 FEVS Technical Report), not the data file's labels**; each of the 93 truncated labels was checked to be a prefix of the report wording for the same q-number, and the labels were used only to confirm the code-to-item tie. The instrument's non-substantive options (Do Not Know / No Basis to Judge / Not Applicable) are unlabelled sentinels dropped by the processing script and so are deliberately absent from `option_text`. Note that `q12` and `q34` are negatively worded and already reverse-coded in the source file, so their anchors run 1 = Strongly Agree to 5 = Strongly Disagree while the other agreement items run the other way
- table: mohammed_2021_job_satisfaction
  issue: |-
    Item text and response anchors are transcribed exactly as the study's SPSS file stores them -- all lowercase, no terminal punctuation, and one item reads "am proud to work at this hospital" with no leading "I". The wording has deliberately not been tidied. The source study never reproduces these five items and never names the instrument: **its identification as the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire job-satisfaction domain is inferred from the wording, not stated by the study**, and the 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree direction rests on the SPSS value labels alone, which nothing else in the study could corroborate
- table: himmelstein-impossible_question-2025
  issue: |-
    **18 of the 90 items (the `IQ_*` codes) are deliberately unanswerable** -- they ask about invented battles, shapes and places, and the correct response is to select "Opt-out". So `resp` = 1 means the respondent either picked the keyed answer or correctly opted out, and `resp` = 0 covers both a wrong answer and opting out of a question that did have one; note that opting out of an answerable item is scored incorrect even though the instructions told participants it would not be scored. `option_text` is empty by design: each trial offered two alternatives plus "Opt-out", but `resp` is a 0/1 correctness score rather than which option was chosen, so the option texts cannot be mapped onto it -- the correct option is given in `correct_response` instead
- table: abukhalaf_2025_disaster_prep
  issue: |-
    **`resp` is a proportion, not an ordinal level**: the source study measured its rising-scale answers and then converted them to percentages, so the 11 values run 0 to 1 in 0.1 steps and mean 0% to 100% likelihood rather than 1st through 11th response option. `option_text` is empty for every row by design -- the source labels no individual point on the slider
- table: mgkt
  issue: |-
    The correct answers were not published with this dataset: the codebook gives each question's text and its ten alternatives but never states which five are correct. The key shipped in correct_response was derived by this project from the response data, not taken from the source. Each MGKT question showed 10 alternatives of which exactly 5 were correct, and respondents checked as many as they knew; the IRW resp is therefore not a chosen option but a per-item score, the number of correct alternatives checked minus the number of incorrect ones (-5 to 5), which is why option_text is blank. correct_response lists the five correct alternatives for each question as text, not as resp values. Note that the administered instructions shipped here state a -1.25 penalty per wrong answer (the feedback scoring on the test page), while the score stored in the IRW table applies a penalty of exactly 1 per wrong answer; this was confirmed against the released raw data for all 32 items. The five incorrect decoy alternatives per question are not shipped here but are listed in the source codebook.
- table: psychoneurotic_inventory
  issue: |-
    The instructions shipped with this table are the study site's own wording and state that the inventory has 112 yes/no questions; the deposit and the response data both contain 116 items (1-116).
- table: chatton2024_honos13
  issue: |-
    The HoNOS-13 was administered in French; no French wording was deposited, so the English item names printed in the source paper's Table 1 are shipped in their place, and the 0-4 response anchors come from the Royal College of Psychiatrists' HoNOS glossary rather than from the study, which labels only the two endpoints.
- table: chen2022_cls
  issue: |-
    Item wording is the canonical English CLS and refers to the school context, while the study administered a Chinese version and interprets the scale as loneliness at home; the six reverse-worded items (A1, A4, A8, A10, A16, A22) are stored already reverse-scored, so their response labels run in descending order (resp 1 = 'Always true').
- table: chen2022b_selfesteem
  issue: |-
    Responses in this table are stored already direction-aligned (higher = higher self-esteem), so the 1-4 codes do not share one anchor orientation across the ten items; the paper's stated anchor direction is contradicted by its own data, so no response-option wording is shipped. Item text is the authors' English rendering of the items, taken verbatim from their data file's column headers (source typos retained); the instrument was administered in Chinese and no Chinese wording is published in the article or the deposit.
- table: chen2022b_socsupport
  issue: |-
    Item text is the canonical English MSPSS wording; the study administered a Chinese version and no Chinese wording is published in the paper or its data deposit, and the anchors for scale points 2-6 are the canonical MSPSS labels rather than ones the study printed.
- table: chen_2021_acculturation
  issue: |-
    The BAS-MBIW was administered orally in Mandarin Chinese; the item wording shown is the authors' own published English, as no Chinese-language version appears in the article or its single supplementary file. Note also that responses are stored 1-5 while the paper scores the scale 0-4, and that the paper's Table 1 names the anchors 'rarely...usually' where the data file's own value labels read 'never...always' (the latter are shipped).
- table: chen_2021_enculturation
  issue: |-
    The BAS-MBIW was administered as a Mandarin Chinese interview (with an interpreter where needed), but no Chinese wording is published in the paper or its S1 Data file, so the item text shown is the English wording carried in the data file's own SPSS variable labels. Note also that the published scale is scored 0-4 (never..always) while the IRW table stores 1-5, so the anchors here are attached to the shifted coding.
- table: weber2026_name_knowledge
  issue: |-
    `item_text`, `option_text` and `instructions` carry the administered German; the English in the `_translated` columns is the authors' own, published in the same record, rather than an IRW rendering. The 1-5 response direction follows the order the printed questionnaire shows its checkboxes in: the study's data file stores unlabelled integers with no value labels, so the direction could not be confirmed against the data and rests on the instrument alone.
- table: boudreau_2022_police_reform
  issue: |-
    `resp` is not fully ordinal. Levels 1-4 run from strongly support to strongly oppose, but level 5 is "Don't know", which the questionnaire offered alongside the four substantive options and which about 11% of respondents chose on every item. Treating 5 as the oppose end of the scale will mis-order the data. Separately coded no-answer responses are dropped, as in the source.
- table: kushnir2017_anrt
  issue: |-
    The `item` code is the source file's full column header, so the join key contains the item wording itself; `item_text` is that same wording with the "(ANRT_n)" prefix removed. Respondents could also answer "Don't know", which the source drops rather than codes, so between 8% and 16% of responses per item are absent from the table and are not missing at random -- the five levels here come from six that were offered. The stem that says what "these products" refers to is not published in the source record; per the IRW dictionary the referent is nicotine replacement therapy, but that is not transcribed text.
- table: balmas2018_leader_personality
  issue: |-
    Eleven of these items are bipolar adjective pairs rated 1-5 (for example "Untrustworthy-Trustworthy"), and the study's codebook labels only the two poles, so `option_text` is present at 1 and 5 and blank at 2-4 by design. Bracketed alternatives in the text -- `[Germany; Israel]`, `[US; Israel]` -- are the study's own notation, not an IRW artifact: the same item went to a US sample and an Israeli sample with the country substituted, and it ships unresolved, so the wording here is not what either group saw verbatim. All items are oriented positive-high as published and none were reverse coded; the codebook's don't-know/no-answer code is dropped, matching the 1-5 range shipped.
- table: balmas2018_leader_attitudes
  issue: |-
    Only the poles of each 1-5 scale are labelled, following the study's codebook, so `option_text` is present at 1 and 5 and blank at 2-4. Bracketed alternatives such as `[US; Israel]` and `[America's; Israel's]` are the study's own notation for its two samples and ship unresolved, so the item text is not what either group saw verbatim.
- table: lee2024_relative_clause
  issue: |-
    The source test has 25 items; only items 1-18 are in this table. Items 19-25 were a separate grammaticality-judgement task with a different response format and were not carried over. The items are in English by design -- this is a test of English relative clauses given to Korean high-schoolers -- while the printed instructions carried Korean glosses, transcribed as printed. Items 1-3 are a picture-circling task and items 4-18 read-and-answer, each with its own administered direction, and `item_text` gives the stimulus sentence together with its comprehension question, as they were administered. Source typos are kept verbatim.
- table: Adherence_Zissette_2018_SDB
  issue: |-
    These 26 items are a Marlowe-Crowne-derived social desirability scale embedded in a much longer HIV-trial screening questionnaire. The item codes are the screener's numbering, not the scale's, which is why they fall in three non-consecutive blocks (q_s_025-032, q_s_056-063, q_s_084-093) rather than a single run. The 1-6 anchors ("Disagree a Lot" to "Agree a Lot") are the study's own; its missing-data code is dropped rather than shipped as a response level.
- table: hypersensitive_narcissism
  issue: |-
    The table is named for the Hypersensitive Narcissism Scale but holds 22 items from two instruments: the 10-item HSNS (items 1-10) followed by the 12-item Dirty Dozen (items 11-22, in the order psychopathy, narcissism, Machiavellianism -- the column order of the source data file, which is not the order its codebook lists them in). Both were administered on the same 1-5 scale in the Open-Source Psychometrics Project's Dark Triad Personality Test, which labels only 1 (disagree), 3 (neutral) and 5 (agree), so `option_text` is blank at 2 and 4. The item codes are bare integers assigned by IRW processing; the source's own codes (HSNS1-10, DDM/DDP/DDN1-4) are not carried in the table. The IRW dictionary entry for this table describes and cites only the HSNS and is being corrected separately.
- table: machivallianism_test_vcl
  issue: |-
    This table is not the Machiavellianism scale: it is the 16-word vocabulary check-list administered in the same openpsychometrics session as the MACH-IV, in which respondents ticked every word whose definition they were sure they knew (1 = checked, 0 = unchecked). VCL6 "cuivocal", VCL9 "florted" and VCL12 "verdid" are deliberate non-words the study included as a validity check, not transcription errors, and should not be corrected to real words. `correct_response` is blank for all 16 items because the source publishes no scoring key.
- table: short_dark_triad
  issue: |-
    The item codes are bare integers 1-27 assigned by IRW processing; the source's own codes, which name the subscale each item belongs to, are not carried in the table. In code order, items 1-9 are Machiavellianism, 10-18 Narcissism and 19-27 Psychopathy. The deposit states only three of the five scale anchors (1 = disagree, 3 = neutral, 5 = agree), so `option_text` is blank at 2 and 4 rather than padded, and it records no participant-facing instructions, so `instructions` is empty.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_det_core
  issue: |-
    The study's deposit publishes these 13 statements twice, under two different numberings: the pilot-1 questionnaire and the pilot-1 codebook order them differently, and only 3 of the 13 positions agree. The released data follow the codebook, so the item text here is the codebook's wording and numbering; it differs in minor wording from the questionnaire respondents were handed, and for some items may be a later revision of it. Both pilots were administered to Brazilian students in Brazilian Portuguese and no Portuguese wording appears anywhere in the deposit, so the text shown is the authors' English original and the `_translated` columns are empty -- the standard's signal that the base fields are not what respondents read.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_genom_know
  issue: |-
    Despite the table name, `resp` here is not a correctness score: it is the raw 4-point agreement scale the first pilot administered (1 = strongly disagree to 4 = strongly agree), so `option_text` is meaningful. `correct_response` accordingly holds the agreement levels the study's codebook counts as understanding -- "3;4" where the statement is true, "1;2" where it is false -- rather than a single keyed option. "Don't know" was an offered response that IRW processing drops as non-response rather than scoring it wrong, so per-item n varies with item difficulty and is lowest on the five statements that mention epigenetics. As with `carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_det_core`, the deposit numbers these 18 statements two different ways and the shipped text follows the codebook, which is the numbering the data demonstrably use. The pilot was administered in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes no Portuguese wording, so the English original ships with the `_translated` columns empty.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_traits
  issue: |-
    This is the first pilot's table-of-traits matrix: 20 traits, each rated 1-5, with the shared stem and rubric recorded once in `instructions` rather than repeated into every item. Respondents could also mark a sixth "don't know" column, which IRW processing drops, so it has no `resp` level here. The questionnaire's worked example row is not an item and is excluded. `correct_response` is blank: the codebook publishes an expected answer per trait, but it is a scientific reference value for a belief item rather than a response key. The pilot was administered to Brazilian students in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes only English, so the item and option text is the authors' English original and the `_translated` columns are empty -- the standard's signal that the base fields are not the wording respondents read.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot2_attitudes
  issue: |-
    Six of these 20 items are negatively worded and the study's codebook reverses them before scoring; they are stored **raw** here, so anyone summing or averaging the scale must reverse them first. `resp` is the codebook's primary coding as administered (1 = strongly disagree to 4 = strongly agree), not its secondary "very negative to very positive" recode. The second pilot was administered to Brazilian students in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes no Portuguese wording, so the item and option text is the authors' English original and the `_translated` columns are empty.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot2_det_core
  issue: |-
    `resp` is a correctness score, not the answer the respondent gave: participants chose True, False or Don't know, and the study's own key scores the keyed answer 1 and the other 0. IRW processing drops "Don't know" and missing as non-response rather than scoring them incorrect -- narrower than the study's own codebook, which scores don't-know as 0 -- so a 0 here always means a wrong True/False answer, and "Don't know" has no `resp` level of its own. `option_text` names which literal choice each score corresponds to on each item. The second pilot was administered to Brazilian students in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes no Portuguese wording, so the text is the authors' English original and the `_translated` columns are empty.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot2_genom_know
  issue: |-
    `resp` is not the response the student gave but a correctness score: each of these 16 statements was asked as True / False / Don't know, and IRW processing records 1 where the answer matches the study's own published key and 0 where it does not. `option_text` is therefore blank throughout by design, and `correct_response` holds the keyed answer ("True" or "False") rather than a `resp` value. Don't-know and missing responses are dropped as non-response rather than scored incorrect -- narrower than the study's own codebook -- so per-item n runs from 35 to 70 of the 78 respondents and is lowest on the five statements about epigenetics, which the paper itself reports drew the most don't-knows. The items were administered in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes only English, which is what ships here, with the `_translated` columns empty.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot2_traits
  issue: |-
    This is the second pilot's table-of-traits matrix: 17 traits, each rated 1-5, with the shared stem in `instructions` rather than repeated into every item. It is a different trait list from the first pilot's, which has 20 and includes a sixth "don't know" column this form does not. `correct_response` is blank, since the pilot-2 codebook publishes no expected answer for the trait matrix. The pilot was administered to Brazilian students in Brazilian Portuguese and the deposit publishes only English, so the item and option text is the authors' English original and the `_translated` columns are empty -- the standard's signal that the base fields are not the wording respondents read.
- table: COACH_Chen_2022_ADL
  issue: |-
    The COACH trial was conducted in Chinese, but no Chinese wording is deposited; the item and response text shown is the study codebook's own English rendering. Item ra_adl_q9 is labelled 'Washing' in that codebook, but respondents report more difficulty with it than with 'Bathing' (ra_adl_q10), so the underlying item is likely doing laundry rather than personal washing.
- table: COACH_Chen_2022_CSQ
  issue: |-
    This table is dictionary-described as the 8-item Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8), but its items are not that instrument: they are items 1-8 of Baker's Consultation Satisfaction Questionnaire short form (CSQ-9), rated 1 'Strongly agree' to 5 'Strongly disagree', taken verbatim from the study's own codebook. The two reverse-worded items (q3 and q8) are stored raw, and the wording shipped is the deposit's English codebook text -- the questionnaire was administered in Chinese, and no Chinese wording appears anywhere in the deposit.
- table: COACH_Chen_2022_IADL
  issue: |-
    Item and option wording is the English text of the study's own codebook; the trial was administered in Chinese and the administered wording is not published in the deposit or the paper. The eight IADL items deliberately have different numbers of response options (three to five), which is how the Lawton IADL is written, so the shipped option text is keyed correctly item by item. Separately, 65 of the table's 54,653 responses (0.12%) hold a value above their own item's maximum and therefore carry no option text; these occur only at the 6- and 12-month waves, and at baseline every item's largest observed value equals its expected ceiling.
- table: COACH_Chen_2022_MOS_SSS_C
  issue: |-
    The 19 MOS Social Support Survey items are shipped against the questionnaire's own numbering (Sherbourne & Stewart 1991) rather than the study codebook's. That codebook lists the items grouped by subscale and numbers them Q2-Q20 in that grouped order, but the responses match the canonical numbering: the four tangible-support items are q2, q5, q12 and q15, which load 0.70-0.81 on their own factor and are the four highest-mean items in all three waves (3.96/3.93/3.91/3.76 against 2.62-3.04), where the codebook would place them at q10-q13. The order of items within a subscale is not independently confirmed. The wording shown is the English original; the survey was administered in Chinese and no Chinese text appears anywhere in the deposit.
- table: chinvararak_2021_phq15
  issue: |-
    Item text and instructions are the PHQ-15's canonical English wording, not the Thai the 180 respondents actually read: the PLOS deposit and supplements contain only 2-4 word Thai keyword tags as SPSS variable labels, never the Thai stems, so `language` is set to Thai beside an empty `item_text_translated` to mark the table for a later backfill. The response options are genuine administered Thai (ไม่รบกวน / รบกวนเล็กน้อย / รบกวนมาก = 0/1/2), taken from the deposit's own value labels.
- table: choy_2022_extraneous_events
  issue: |-
    The four item wordings come from the paper's Table 1, which prints them as an unnumbered list, so their assignment to the codes Extraneous1-Extraneous4 rests on presentation order; a CFA on the live data reproduces the paper's published Extraneous loadings (.67/.77/.82/.85 vs .67/.76/.83/.85) and confirms the codes match the paper's item numbering, but not that the list is in that order.
- table: chuemchit_2024_nonpartner_violence
  issue: |-
    Each of the five items is an author-derived binary indicator summarising several separate questionnaire questions, not one question: the `item_text` shipped here is the authors' own definition of that violence type (from the paper's Methods), and the study publishes no key saying which of the 14 non-partner questions (S1 File Q126-Q191) feed each indicator. The interviews were conducted in Khmer, Lao and Myanmar; only the English questionnaire version is deposited, so the shipped wording is not the string respondents heard.
- table: chuemchit_2024_partner_violence
  issue: |-
    The five items are derived binary indicators, each collapsing 2-4 questionnaire questions of one violence type crossed with a 'in the last 12 months' follow-up, so `item_text` quotes the constituent questions rather than a single stem. The survey was administered orally in Lao, Burmese and Khmer and only the English master questionnaire was published, so the shipped wording is an English substitute for what respondents heard.
- table: cinar_tanriverdi_2023_gad7
  issue: |-
    `item_text` ships the Turkish wording of the GAD-7 adaptation the study used (Konkan et al. 2013). The English in the `_translated` columns is Pfizer's official GAD-7 wording for the same numbered items, not a word-for-word translation of that Turkish -- the two diverge, for example Turkish item 1 is phrased as a direct question and item 6 adds a restlessness clause. No administered instruction line is shipped because none of the study's sources print one.
- table: cogcontrol_gyurkovics_2019_flanker
  issue: |-
    Item text for this table was reconstructed by IRW, not transcribed: the OSF deposit identifies each stimulus only by a numeric image id and ships no stimulus images, so the arrow display and correct keypad key shown for each item were decoded from the trial-level data (two independent columns agreeing across all 118 participants); the arrows are a rendering of images the deposit does not include, and no verbatim participant instructions are published.
- table: cogcontrol_gyurkovics_2019_sart
  issue: |-
    The item text for this table is the stimulus digit itself, which is all a SART trial presents; no verbatim participant instructions are published by the study, so the `instructions` field is empty, and `option_text` holds the deposit's accuracy codes (0 incorrect / 1 correct) rather than response options participants read.
- table: cogcontrol_gyurkovics_2019_simon
  issue: |-
    Item text for this table was reconstructed by IRW, not transcribed: the OSF deposit identifies each Simon stimulus only by a numeric image id and ships no stimulus images, so the arrow direction, its screen location and the correct keypad key shown for each item were decoded from the trial-level data (correct-trial key code, 100% pure across 34,338 trials, plus the congruency column and the deposit's own feature-repetition code); the arrows are a rendering of images the deposit does not include, and no verbatim participant instructions are published.
- table: colomer_perez_2021_soc13
  issue: |-
    Item text is the canonical English SOC-13 (Antonovsky Orientation to Life Questionnaire) wording; the study administered a Spanish version whose wording is not reproduced in the paper or its data deposit, and the deposited .sav carries no labels tying its INVSOC1-SOC13 codes to individual items, so the mapping rests on the code numbering plus a scoring check that pins each item's polarity but not its position within a polarity class. Responses are stored raw, not reverse-scored, so for items 1, 2, 3, 7 and 10 a high value means a lower sense of coherence. Only the two extreme scale points are labelled on the instrument; points 2-6 are intentionally blank.
- table: conner_2017_bfi
  issue: |-
    IRW does not offer item text for this table. In the response data, sixteen of the 44
    items (BFI 2, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 31, 34, 35, 37, 41, 43) are stored
    already reverse-scored, so for those items a low `resp` indicates agreement with the
    item as worded
- table: conner_2017_cesd
  issue: |-
    Items 4, 8, 12 and 16 are stored already reverse scored, so their response anchors are shipped in reverse order (`resp` 0 = 'Most or all of the time') relative to how the positively-worded stem reads; this matches the numbers in the response data.
- table: conner_2017_curiosity
  issue: |-
    Item wording is transcribed verbatim from the study's own SPSS file, so it preserves that file's wording rather than the published Curiosity and Exploration Inventory-II: item 1 reads "I actively seeks as much information as I can in a new situation" where the published CEI-II reads "I actively seek ... in new situations", and items 1 and 8 carry a trailing full stop the other eight lack. The source file also labels the block "Curiousity and Engagement Inventory II"; the `instrument` field ships the correct name (Kashdan et al. 2009), which the paper's own reference 47 confirms.
- table: conner_2017_vitality
  issue: |-
    The IRW dictionary describes this table as the Subjective Vitality Scale; the items are in fact the modified 4-item energy/fatigue (Vitality) subscale of the RAND SF-36, and items 3 and 4 ("worn out", "tired") are stored already reverse-scored, so a response of 100 on those items means "None of the time".
- table: promis1wave1_cesd
  issue: |-
    The 20-item CES-D. resp runs 0-3 from 'Rarely or none of the time (Less than 1 day)' to 'Most or all of the time (5-7 days)', one shared response set across every item. Items 4, 8, 12 and 16 are positively worded and so score in reverse of the other sixteen.
- table: promis1wave1_haq
  issue: |-
    The HAQ disability items. 20 items ask how much difficulty an activity caused over the past week, resp 0-3 from 'Without any difficulty' to 'Unable to do'; the other 4 (HAQ9-HAQ12) ask whether an aid or another person is usually needed and are yes/no, resp 0-1. The numeric prefix marks the instrument's activity category, so HAQ1a and HAQ1b are two items about the same category.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_ia
  issue: |-
    Item text and the response ladder are the administered English wording of the COVIDiSTRESS Round II form. resp runs 1-10 on a slider whose ends only are labelled, 1 = 'Not at all' and 10 = 'Frequently'; the eight intermediate positions had no verbal label and so carry none here. Items are tied to codes by the form's listing order.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_distrust
  issue: |-
    Item text and the 7-point agreement ladder (Strongly disagree, Disagree, Slightly disagree, Neutral, Slightly agree, Agree, Strongly agree) are the administered English wording. The 6 misperception items are matched by the form's own B.x.y numbering; the 4 conspiratorial-thinking and 3 anti-expert items by listing order. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_dtl
  issue: |-
    Item text and both ladders are the administered English wording. The table pools two different scales: the 6 resilience items run 1-7 on an agreement ladder, and the 5 uncertainty items run 1-5 on a 'characteristic of me' ladder, so resp is not comparable across the two blocks -- read section_id and option_text rather than assuming one scale. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_identity
  issue: |-
    Item text is the administered English wording. resp 0-6 is a 7-point agreement scale whose midpoint the cleaned data recodes to 0: 0 = Neutral, then 1 = Strongly disagree through 6 = Strongly agree. Note that 0 is therefore the MIDDLE of the scale, not its bottom. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_moral
  issue: |-
    Item text is the administered English wording. resp 0-6 is a 7-point agreement scale whose midpoint the cleaned data recodes to 0: 0 = Neutral, then 1 = Strongly disagree through 6 = Strongly agree. Note that 0 is the MIDDLE of the scale, not its bottom. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_sscd
  issue: |-
    Item text and ladders are the administered English wording; the compliance items are past tense as administered. item_family separates compliance (1) from injunctive norms (2) and descriptive norms (3), and the three blocks use different ladders, so resp is not comparable across them. The norm ladders label only their ends, so their intermediate positions carry no option_text. Item 7 of each block is reverse-worded ('Met with people outside of your household for non-essential reasons') and runs against the other seven. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_stress
  issue: |-
    Item text and ladders are the administered English wording. The table pools three blocks with two ladders: the Perceived Stress Scale on 0 = Never to 4 = Very often, and both stressor blocks on 0 = Not at all concerned to 4 = Very concerned. Two secondary-stressor items, indices 8 and 9, carry only 6 and 8 responses against about 9,700 for the rest of their block, which is a defect in the source's display logic rather than in the item text. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_vaccine
  issue: |-
    Item text and ladders are the administered English wording, including the form's typo 'how wiling you were' in the willingness item. The table pools two scales: willingness on resp 0-4, where 0 is the Neutral midpoint, 1 = 'Not willing at all' and 4 = 'Very willing' with two unlabelled positions between; and 6 attitude items on resp 0-6, where 0 is the Neutral midpoint and 1-6 run Strongly disagree to Strongly agree. The attitude codes are numbered 2-6 and 9, so three of the instrument's attitude positions are absent from the data. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_emotion
  issue: |-
    The Emotion Regulation Questionnaire short form, 8 items: expressive suppression (items 1, 2, 4 and 5) and cognitive reappraisal (3, 6, 7 and 8). resp 0-6 is a 7-point agreement scale whose midpoint the cleaned data recodes to 0, so 0 = Neutral, 1 = Strongly disagree and 6 = Strongly agree; the form labelled only those three positions, so the four between them carry no option_text. Unlike its ten sibling tables this one really is the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire the dataset description names.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_support
  issue: |-
    Three perceived-social-support items. resp 0-6 is a 7-point agreement scale whose midpoint the cleaned data recodes to 0: 0 = Neutral, then 1 = Strongly disagree through 6 = Strongly agree. Note that 0 is the MIDDLE of the scale, not its bottom. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: ecps_sahm_2024_trust
  issue: |-
    Seven institutional-trust items. resp 0-10 is a percentage slider in ten-point steps: 0 = 'No trust', then 10% at resp 1 through 90% at resp 9. The form's label for the top position is not recoverable from the deposited PDF, so resp 10 carries no option_text, though the arithmetic of the scale makes it 100%. Note on the table name: the `ecps_sahm_2024_` prefix points at Sahm et al.'s German Emotion Regulation Questionnaire validation, which is not what this table is. These responses are the COVIDiSTRESS Global Survey Round II; its cleaned data file is hosted inside that study's OSF project, which is how the two came to be conflated. The name is kept because renaming a published table breaks every existing reference to it.
- table: conspiracy_asd__cognitive_flexibility
  issue: |-
    Item wording here comes from the deposit's plain-text survey document, not from the coded Qualtrics workbook that accompanies it. That workbook's label row is corrupted by a global find/replace of 'no' to '2' -- it reads 'I feel I have 2 power' and 'I just don't k2w what to do' -- so anyone comparing this table against those labels will find differences. The plain-text document agrees word for word with the uncorrupted labels in the deposit's raw data file.
- table: conspiracy_asd__conspiracy_gcbs
  issue: |-
    The source Excel's question-text header carries a mechanical corruption in which the letters 'no' were replaced by the digit '2' (e.g. 'in2cent', 'tech2logy'); the item text published here reverses that substitution.
- table: conspiracy_asd__schizotypy
  issue: |-
    The item codes are a 37-item sequence, not MSS-B item numbers: the study administered all 38 MSS-B items but its deposited data omit "I believe that dreams have magical properties" (survey item 11), so schizotypy_11 onward are offset by one from the published MSS-B numbering. The transcribed instructions also say to answer "from 1 to 4" while the anchor table beneath them and the data are 1-5.
- table: conspiracy_asd__thinking_styles
  issue: |-
    The instrument is the 10-item Rational-Experiential Inventory short form, administered under the survey's own heading 'Thinking Styles'. Only the two extreme scale points are labelled on the instrument ('completely false' and 'completely true'), so `option_text` is blank for responses 2, 3 and 4 -- those points are genuinely unlabelled rather than missing. Wording is taken from the deposit's plain-text survey document, because the coded workbook's labels carry a find/replace artifact ('k2w' for 'know').
- table: cooper_2018_funny_topics
  issue: |-
    This battery is a select-all-that-apply checklist, so `resp` is a checkbox state rather than a chosen response option, and the `option_text` values 'Selected' and 'Not selected' describe that 0/1 coding rather than transcribing anything the survey printed -- the source publishes no response labels for this battery, only the stem 'Please select all that you might find funny.' Item text and instructions are verbatim from the study's own survey file.
- table: cooper_2018_offensive_topics
  issue: |-
    This battery is a select-all-that-apply checklist, so `resp` is a checkbox state rather than a chosen response option, and the `option_text` values 'Selected' and 'Not selected' describe that 0/1 coding rather than transcribing survey wording -- the source prints no response labels for it. Item text is verbatim from the study's own survey file.
- table: cormier_2024_personality
  issue: |-
    IRW does not offer item text for this table: the wording was the BFI-2-XS, withdrawn under the
    2026-09-10 ruling that the BFI-2's non-commercial-only terms block it. In the response data,
    item Q20_8 is not a personality item but an attention check instructing respondents to select
    'Agree Strongly', and every respondent did (all 898 responses are 5). Exclude it before
    scoring the BFI-2-XS.
- table: cormier_2024_phq4
  issue: |-
    The source Qualtrics export concatenates a shared block stem with each item stem in one header, joined by ' - '. That shared stem is shipped once in `instructions` and `item_text` holds only the per-item sentence, so an item here is shorter than the corresponding column header in the source file.
- table: CPDMMC_Kunnari_2020_HCD
  issue: |-
    The codebook this table follows keys `VT` to the Vaccine dilemma and `V` to the Vitamins dilemma, which reads backwards at a glance; the assignment is the study's own and is transcribed as published. Only the endpoint anchors are labelled (1 = Not acceptable at all, 7 = Totally acceptable) because the deposit labels no others, and `instructions` is blank because no literal instruction text is published anywhere in the deposit.
- table: CPDMMC_Kunnari_2020_PDP
  issue: |-
    Two wordings that look like transcription errors are the source's and were kept verbatim: the `CA_C`/`CA_IC` vignettes read 'too fast to break in time' (for 'brake'), and `VP_C` reads 'sideeffects'. Each item carries its own `section_prompt` rather than sharing one, because the congruent and incongruent versions of a dilemma are different scenarios; where the source vignette repeated its judgment question inside the paragraph, that duplicate sentence was dropped so the question appears once, in `item_text`.
- table: CQTMS_Hur_2023
  issue: |-
    Item text covers only 79 of the 160 items -- the study published wording for the finally selected items only, so the other 81 ship blank `item_text`; of the 79, 30 have Korean wording with no English translation because the article's English supplement omits three of the eight character qualities. The 5-point response anchors are shipped in English (the Korean anchors were never published) and describe the raw scale direction stored in the table, which is the opposite of the reverse-scored distributions the article's Supplement 1 reports for 17 negatively-worded items.
- table: corti_2023_academic_adaptation
  issue: |-
    The 1-5 response anchors are not shipped: neither the study's SPSS deposit nor the paper publishes the labels for this five-point scale, so `option_text` is blank and the direction of the scale is not documented by the source.
- table: cox_2024_feedback_perceptions
  issue: |-
    Only three response anchors are shipped for what the study describes as a five-point scale: no respondent ever used 1 (never) or 2 (once in a while), so those values do not occur in the table and only the sometimes/often/almost always anchors appear. Item text is the source spreadsheet's column headers verbatim, minus their PreQ#/PostQ# wave prefixes -- one item code spans both waves -- with three run-together words separated ('feedbackin', 'throughoutyour', 'memberin').
- table: cucchi_2018_kims
  issue: |-
    Item codes KIMS1-18 are this study's own renumbering of the 39-item KIMS Describing (1-8) and Acting with Awareness (9-18) subscales; they are not canonical KIMS item numbers.
- table: cucchi_2018_rfq
  issue: |-
    The source file's response anchors for RFQ1 differ from the other seven items in casing and read 'somehow agree' where the rest read 'Agree somewhat'; the shipped anchors use the wording the other seven items carry.
- table: cucchi_2018_scoff
  issue: |-
    Items SCOFF2, SCOFF3 and SCOFF4 ship without a terminal question mark and SCOFF1 and SCOFF5 with one, because that is how the source data file's variable labels write them -- not an omission to be tidied. `instructions` and `section_prompt` are blank because neither the paper nor the deposit publishes any administration instructions for the SCOFF.
- table: cugmas_2021_elderly_social_support
  issue: |-
    `resp` here is a count of network members, not a rated response: each item is one relationship type and the value is how many people of that type the respondent named across the survey's three social-support name generators, so there are no response-option labels. Note also that the study's English-language questionnaire (S2) lists 14 relationship categories while the Slovenian questionnaire actually administered (S1) lists the seven that appear in the data; the seven Slovenian categories are what is published here.
- table: CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020_RSES
  issue: |-
    Item text for this Czech-administered Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale table is the canonical English RSES wording, not the Czech wording respondents actually read -- the OSF deposit and the paper publish neither the Czech items nor any per-item labels. The item codes are reconstructed as the widely circulated RSES ordering (reverse-keyed at 2, 5, 6, 8, 9), not Rosenberg's 1965 ordering, on the basis of the study's own scoring script; that pins each item's polarity class, the response direction and RSES_8, but does not distinguish RSES_3 from RSES_4, RSES_1 from RSES_10, or the four remaining reverse-keyed items from one another. Responses are stored raw, with 1 = 'Strongly agree' and 4 = 'Strongly disagree' for every item including the reverse-worded ones.
- table: dahlstrom_2022_scoare
  issue: |-
    Six items (SF, SD, ST, SM, KE, KA) were asked only in the workshop's first program year, whose survey version PLOS does not publish; they carry the second-year form's parent stem without its 'scientific writing' / 'speaking or presenting' qualifier.
- table: daiku_2021_dirty_dozen
  issue: |-
    The DTDD-J was administered in Japanese; `item_text_translated` reproduces Jonason and Webster's (2010) original English for the correspondingly numbered items, but the English shown for the instructions and for the two scale anchors was translated by IRW rather than by the study's authors.
- table: dalky_2020_sf36
  issue: |-
    This SF-36 was administered in Arabic; the item and option wording shipped here is the study's own English rendering, taken from its SPSS variable and value labels, not the Arabic wording respondents read (the deposit publishes no Arabic text). The five block stems are the canonical public-domain RAND-36 English wording, supplied because the data file carries no block headers and many item labels are fragments without them. The table holds 35 of the SF-36's 36 items -- one physical-functioning item and one general-health-perception item are absent from the source file.
- table: dasilva_2019_hexaco24
  issue: |-
    The English in the `_translated` columns is the original Brief HEXACO Inventory wording as reproduced by the study's own paper, not a translation of the Portuguese actually administered; six items (3, 7, 9, 14, 15, 19) and the two 'slightly' anchors differ in wording between the two versions.
- table: dass_Thiyagarajan2022
  issue: |-
    Most of this sample did not read the wording shipped here: the study let participants choose the Bahasa Malaysia or English DASS-21, and 90% of the 971 respondents used the Malay version, but only the English wording appears in the study's deposit or paper.
- table: dd_rotation
  issue: |-
    The items are pictures, not text: each is a display of two 3-D objects and the respondent judges same/different, so `item_text` carries only the stimulus's rotation angle (50, 100 or 150 degrees) as documented in the diffIRT package, and the option labels describe scored accuracy rather than the yes/no button the respondent pressed.
- table: debacker_2018_decisionjustification
  issue: |-
    The paper's Measures section states items were answered on a 5-point scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree), but the deposited data are coded 0-5 and all six levels are used (e.g. item 1: 6/28/69/123/267/175), so the published anchor labels cannot be attached to specific `resp` values; `option_text` is left blank.
- table: de_vries_2022_bat_burnout_core
  issue: |-
    The Dutch wording shipped here is the official work-related Burnout Assessment Tool questionnaire, not text published by this study: the study's own deposit carries no variable or value labels for any BAT column and the paper prints only two example items.
