- table: zeng_2026_gai_role_adapt
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    published in the paper, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zeng_2026_gai_self_efficacy
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    published in the paper, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zeng_2026_gai_ttf
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    published in the paper, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2020_trait_creativity_mood
  issue: |-
    Item tired.1 is labelled 'tired' in the source data file (a duplicated column
    header); the paper lists that mood item as 'sleepy', and it is assigned 'sleepy'
    here because it sits sixth in the file, where the paper lists 'sleepy', and the
    file's first five mood columns follow the paper's item order (the last four do not)
    -- the two 'tired' columns correlate 0.74 and the data cannot confirm which is
    which. Wording is the paper's English rendering; the questionnaire was presumably
    administered in Chinese.
- table: zhang_2024_attractiveness
  issue: |-
    Item wording is the authors' English version of a questionnaire administered in
    Chinese, and each wording is matched to its item code only by its number in the
    paper's appendix; the data cannot confirm that match.
- table: zhang_2024_gift_intention
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    from the paper's appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2024_parasocial
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    published in the paper's S1 Appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2024_streamer_dsp
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text is the authors' English from the paper's
    appendix, and because the paper says this scale was reverse-scored before analysis
    (the stored values match the paper's post-reversal statistics) while the Chinese
    wording was not released, it cannot be determined whether resp 5 means agreement or
    disagreement with the English statements shown, so no response labels are given.
- table: zhang_2024_viewer_dsp
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    published in the paper's S1 Appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released, and
    each wording is matched to its item code only by its number in that appendix.
- table: zhang_2025_coercive_pressure
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    from the paper's appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2025_environ_awareness
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    from the paper's appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2025_normative_pressure
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    from the paper's appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhang_2025_self_efficacy
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the authors' own English rendering
    from the paper's appendix, as the Chinese wording was not released.
- table: zhao_2024_erq
  issue: |-
    The ERQ was administered in Chinese (the ERQ-C translation of Wang et al.), but
    neither the PLOS ONE paper nor its data supplement contains any item wording in
    either language -- the data columns are bare codes ERQr1-ERQr10 -- so the item text
    shown here is Gross and John's (2003) canonical English ERQ rather than the
    sentences participants read. Item codes follow the instrument's printed item
    numbers; the reappraisal (r) / suppression (s) split is confirmed by the data and
    every code reproduces the paper's published factor loadings, but nothing in the data
    distinguishes items within a subscale by wording. Scale points 2, 3, 5 and 6 carry
    no option text because the ERQ form labels only 1, 4 and 7.
- table: zhao_2025_digital_literacy
  issue: |-
    Administered in Chinese (CFPS); the item text is the authors' English description
    from the paper, as the Chinese wording was not released. The paper's Table 2 swaps
    the descriptions of digital_social and digital_entertainment relative to its own
    column names and Methods text; the item text here follows the column names
    (digital_social = socializing).
- table: zhao_2025_nat_env_perception
  issue: |-
    Administered in person at a botanical garden in Changsha, presumably in Chinese (the
    paper does not name the language); the item text shown is the authors' English
    wording from the paper's Table 1, the only wording published, and the paper gives no
    response-option labels.
- table: zhao_2025_place_attachment
  issue: |-
    Administered in person at a botanical garden in Changsha, presumably in Chinese (the
    paper does not name the language); the item text shown is the authors' English
    wording from the paper's Table 1, the only wording published, and the paper gives no
    response-option labels.
- table: zhao_2025_psych_recovery_eval
  issue: |-
    Administered in person at a botanical garden in Changsha, presumably in Chinese (the
    paper does not name the language); the item text shown is the authors' English
    wording from the paper's Table 1, the only wording published, and the paper gives no
    response-option labels.
- table: zhou_2024_smart_home_intention
  issue: |-
    Administered to older adults in China, presumably in Chinese; the paper and its data
    file carry only the authors' English wording, which is what is shown here. The
    construct coded ITS is intergenerational technical support (children's help with the
    smart home), not intention to switch.
- table: zhou_2025_ehealth_literacy
  issue: |-
    Administered to university students in China, presumably in Chinese; the study's
    data file carries only the authors' English wording of the eHealth Literacy Scale,
    which is what is shown here, and the paper names only the two end anchors of the
    5-point scale.
- table: AOMT_BR_SF_EDPANAB_Geiger_2021_RF
  issue: |-
    The shipped wording is the English version read by the 259 North American
    respondents; the 248 Bulgarian respondents answered a validated Bulgarian
    translation, and in the North American survey the disease problems (RCG4, RCL2)
    named the respondent's own country, shown here as 'Canada/the United States'.
- table: CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020_PANAS
  issue: |-
    Item text for this Czech-administered PANAS table is the canonical English Watson,
    Clark & Tellegen (1988) adjectives and response anchors, not the Czech wording
    respondents read, which the study does not publish; the adjectives are assigned by
    the canonical item order, which the data confirm to the level of positive/negative
    subscale (with 'alert' behaving like a negative-affect item in this sample, as the
    authors note) but which nothing in the source confirms item by item within a
    subscale.
- table: ALSECYPIAMH_WU_2022_PHQ
  issue: |-
    The item text, the 'Over the last 2 weeks' stem and the 0-3 'Not at all' to 'Nearly every day'
    options are the standard published PHQ-2 wording, not the study's own materials. The study's raw
    data file carries no item labels and its paper is paywalled, so the wording respondents actually
    read could not be confirmed against the study.
- table: APFCompact_Ptacek_2024_DASS-21
  issue: |-
    The item text is the canonical English DASS-21 wording, but the study administered a Czech
    translation that is not published in its OSF deposit or paper, so these are not the sentences
    respondents read. The item codes are the deposit's own column headers, which carry the canonical
    DASS-21 item number and subscale letter.
- table: IJLS_Eersel_2024_DenialAcceptance
  issue: |-
    The four Brief COPE denial and acceptance items were administered in Dutch, but the Dutch
    wording is not published in the DataverseNL deposit or the paper's supplements, so the item and
    option text here is the study's own English rendering from its SPSS labels rather than what
    respondents read. The item codes BC_2, BC_7, BC_10 and BC_12 are this study's administered
    numbering, not the Brief COPE-28's canonical denial (3, 8) and acceptance (20, 24) item numbers.
- table: IJLS_Eersel_2024_Work
  issue: |-
    The work centrality, UWES work engagement and commitment items were administered in validated
    Dutch versions, but the Dutch wording is not published in the deposit or the paper's
    supplements, so the text here is the study's own English rendering from its SPSS labels rather
    than what respondents read. The article describes work engagement as rated 1 = never to 6 =
    always, but the SPSS file labels the three UWES items on a 7-point Never..Always scale and the
    data use all seven levels; the shipped anchors are the file's. WorkCen_3R is stored already
    reverse-scored, and its anchors run Strongly agree to Strongly disagree accordingly.
- table: algner2022_oss
  issue: |-
    The study administered a German version of the Oslo Social Support Scale short form, but the
    item text here comes from the English original, not the German respondents read. Only four of
    the six items have text: item 2 is from Algner's paper, items 5 and 6 are the English original
    as quoted by a Chinese validation study, and item 1 is a lower-confidence back-translation from
    a Brazilian adaptation. Items 3 and 4 are blank because no source gives their literal wording.
- table: anh_2026_ai_adoption
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Vietnamese (translated and back-translated), but no
    Vietnamese wording is published in the paper or its only supplement, a numeric data CSV, so the
    item text here is the English source wording the paper prints in its Table 3 rather than the
    sentences respondents read. Table 3 is published only as an image, so the English was
    transcribed by eye and may carry transcription slips in punctuation. Only scale points 1
    (strongly disagree) and 5 (strongly agree) carry labels; points 2-4 are blank.
- table: anh_2026_digitaltrust
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Vietnamese (translated and back-translated), but no
    Vietnamese wording is published in the paper or its only supplement, a numeric data CSV, so the
    item text here is the English source wording the paper prints in its Table 3 rather than the
    sentences respondents read. Table 3 is published only as an image, so the English was
    transcribed by eye. Only scale points 1 (strongly disagree) and 5 (strongly agree) carry labels;
    points 2-4 are blank.
- table: anh_2026_finliteracy
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Vietnamese (translated and back-translated), but no
    Vietnamese wording is published in the paper or its only supplement, a numeric data CSV, so the
    item text here is the English source wording the paper prints in its Table 3 rather than the
    sentences respondents read. Table 3 is published only as an image, so the English was
    transcribed by eye. Only scale points 1 (strongly disagree) and 5 (strongly agree) carry labels;
    points 2-4 are blank.
- table: anh_2026_finsocialization
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Vietnamese (translated and back-translated), but no
    Vietnamese wording is published in the paper or its only supplement, a numeric data CSV, so the
    item text here is the English source wording the paper prints in its Table 3 rather than the
    sentences respondents read. Table 3 is published only as an image, so the English was
    transcribed by eye; the source's own sentence-medial periods (e.g. FS1 'growing up at home. my
    family') are kept as printed. Only scale points 1 (strongly disagree) and 5 (strongly agree)
    carry labels; points 2-4 are blank.
- table: anh_2026_finwellbeing
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Vietnamese (translated and back-translated), but no
    Vietnamese wording is published in the paper or its only supplement, a numeric data CSV, so the
    item text here is the English source wording the paper prints in its Table 3 rather than the
    sentences respondents read. Table 3 is published only as an image, so the English was
    transcribed by eye; the source's own punctuation errors (e.g. FW4 'At the end of the month. I
    have extra money.') are kept as printed. Only scale points 1 (strongly disagree) and 5 (strongly
    agree) carry labels; points 2-4 are blank.
- table: campos_2023_oes
  issue: |-
    This table pools Finnish-language (n=3,614) and Brazilian Portuguese-language (n=3,979)
    administrations of the Orofacial Esthetic Scale, and the item text is the English source
    instrument (Larsson et al. 2010, as reprinted by Campos et al. 2020) rather than either
    administered version; no file in the study's deposit or supplements gives the items in any
    language. The item-to-code mapping is reconstructed rather than stated by the study. The shipped
    English instructions include a clause about tooth replacements (crowns, bridges and implants)
    that the Portuguese instruction omits, so the administered framing was not identical across the
    two halves.
- table: campos_2023_pidaq
  issue: |-
    This table pools Finnish-language (n=3,614) and Brazilian Portuguese-language (n=3,979)
    administrations of the 24-item PIDAQ, and the item text is the English source instrument (Klages
    et al. 2006, as reprinted by Campos et al. 2020) rather than either administered version; no
    file in the study's deposit or supplements gives the items in any language. The English is not a
    word-for-word match to the Portuguese version for every item (it9, it16 and it22 differ in
    content), and the Finnish administration reworded item 22 to be gender-neutral while the
    original wording is shipped. Item codes follow the original interleaved PIDAQ numbering, not the
    subscale-sequential renumbering some validation papers use.
- table: carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_attitudes
  issue: |-
    The item and option wording is the authors' British-English original of the first-pilot PUGGS
    questionnaire (S3 Table), but the first pilot was administered to Brazilian students in a
    Brazilian Portuguese translation that none of the paper's supplements publishes, so this is not
    the wording respondents read. The questionnaire's fifth option, 'don't know', is dropped from
    the response data, so the table has only the four agreement levels.
- table: chen2022_ses
  issue: |-
    The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale wording here is the canonical English original (Rosenberg 1965);
    the study administered a Chinese adaptation (Ji and Yu, 1999) whose wording it does not publish.
    The mapping of items to the file's bare codes A25-A34 is inferred from questionnaire position --
    no source ties an individual code to an individual item, and nothing distinguishes A27 from A28.
    Response options are blank because the deposited values are already keyed toward high
    self-esteem rather than to the paper's stated '1 = very conformity ... 4 = very inconformity'
    anchors, and A34 runs opposite to the other nine (item-rest r = -0.16).
- table: fredrickson_2015_mhcsf
  issue: |-
    The item wording, anchors and instructions are the canonical Keyes MHC-SF form, not the study's
    own materials, which reproduce none. The shipped instructions are the paper form's, including
    'Place a check mark in the box', while this study administered the questionnaire online. Item 6
    is given in the current wording ('that our society is a good place, or is becoming a better
    place, for all people'); Keyes also documents an original wording, and the study does not say
    which its participants saw.
- table: huang_2016_cesd
  issue: |-
    Huang et al. publish no item wording, so the text here is Radloff's (1977) original English
    CES-D, transcribed from a later CC BY reprint, mapped to the deposit's unlabelled CESD_1-CESD_20
    columns by canonical item number. 30 of the 114 participants were assessed in French, and that
    French wording is not published anywhere in the record. Items 4, 8, 12 and 16 are stored already
    reverse-scored, so their frequency anchors run in reverse (resp 0 = 'Most or all of the time')
    relative to how the positively worded stem reads.
- table: ibrahim_2015_sf36
  issue: |-
    Patients completed the questionnaires in Malay or English, but only English SF-36 wording is
    recoverable, so the item stems, instructions and section prompts are RAND's published English
    36-Item Health Survey 1.0 for a partly Malay-language administration. The deposit's columns
    carry no labels, so each code is tied to its wording by the SF-36's own question numbering. The
    response options are the study's own recorded categories, which differ from the published
    instrument in two places: item 1's lowest category reads 'not good' rather than 'Poor', and
    question 11 was administered on four categories rather than the instrument's five (there is no
    'Don't know').
- table: imos_1987
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 1987 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 237 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text
    notation. The official paper's own typo in problem 3 (a_1 x_2 where a_2 x_2 is meant) is kept as
    printed.
- table: imos_1988
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 1988 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 268 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

    paper's own.
- table: imos_1989

- table: imos_1994

- table: imos_1997
  issue: |-

- table: imos_1999
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 1999 paper. The IMO is sat

- table: imos_2001
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2001 paper. The IMO is sat

    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

- table: imos_2004
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2004 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 486 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

    bracketed description of the figure written by IRW in place of the image; the paper's own typo

- table: imos_2005
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2005 paper. The IMO is sat

- table: imos_2006
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2006 paper. The IMO is sat

- table: imos_2008
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2008 paper. The IMO is sat

- table: imos_2009
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2009 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 565 contestants read a translation of this

- table: imos_2010
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2010 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 516 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

    typography that plain text cannot show, so its distinction is visible only in the typeset
    original.
- table: imos_2012
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2012 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 547 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

- table: imos_2013
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2013 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 527 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text

- table: imos_2014
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2014 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 560 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text
    notation. Problem 6's printed 'Note:' paragraph on partial credit is appended to that item's
    text.
- table: imos_2015
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2015 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 577 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text
    notation.
- table: imos_2017
  issue: |-
    The item text is the organisers' official English version of the IMO 2017 paper. The IMO is sat
    in each contestant's own language, so most of the 615 contestants read a translation of this
    wording rather than the English shown here. Typeset mathematics is rendered in plain-text
    notation.
- table: imps2025_hf
  issue: |-
    Item text is blank by design: Hearts and Flowers stimuli are pictures (a red heart or a red
    flower), and the item code names the stimulus and the side it appeared on. The instructions and
    rule prompts are the canonical description of the standard task (Wright & Diamond 2014), not
    this study's own script, which was never published. This study administered the task to groups
    of children on tablets with side-mounted response buttons and a 750 ms (spring: 1,250 ms)
    response deadline, whereas the canonical description is of an individually administered
    touchscreen version.
- table: jung_2018_media_use
  issue: |-
    The survey was run in Korean, Chinese and Japanese (the questionnaires are in the S2-S4 Files,
    question B3); the shipped wording is the study's own English from the paper's Methods, because
    one table cannot carry three administered wordings. The three response labels are the paper's
    collapsed coding: respondents saw four frequency options (not at all, 1-2, 3-4, 5 or more
    times), so resp=3 'more than three times' merges the top two administered categories.
- table: jutte_2024_loneliness
  issue: |-
    The three revised UCLA Loneliness items were administered in German to a Germany-wide panel, but
    neither the study's SPSS deposit (no variable or value labels) nor the paper's supplements
    publish the German wording, so the item text here is the paper's own English rendering rather
    than what respondents read. The paper describes the scale as 1 = never to 7 = very frequently
    while the table stores 0-6, so the anchors are shipped as 0 = never to 6 = very frequently; the
    five intermediate points are unlabelled in the source.
- table: jutte_2024_personality
  issue: |-
    The Big Five single items were administered in German, but the German wording is not published
    in the deposit or the paper's supplements, so the item text here is the English rendering the
    paper prints in its Table 1 rather than what respondents read. The paper states a 1-7 scale
    while the table stores 0-6; only the endpoints are labelled.
- table: kim2020_ams
  issue: |-
    The study published no item wording, so the shipped Korean text is the official Korean Aging
    Males' Symptoms form (Heinemann et al. 2003), not the study's own materials, and the English in
    the _translated columns is the AMS's official English version rather than a translation of the
    Korean. The form is aligned to the data's Q01-Q17 by the AMS's canonical item numbering; that
    alignment reproduces the scale's three-factor structure but does not distinguish items within a
    subscale.
- table: kim_2023_gad7
  issue: |-
    The GAD-7 was administered in Korean, but no Korean wording is published in the paper or its
    SPSS deposit, so the item and option text here is the instrument publisher's official English
    (phqscreeners.com) rather than the sentences respondents read. The shipped instruction is the
    GAD-7's own 'Over the last 2 weeks', while the paper's Methods describes its GAD-7 as asking
    about anxiety over the past two months. The deposit's columns are unlabelled, so codes are tied
    to wording by the form's printed numbering; data checks pin gad5 (restlessness) and gad6
    (irritability) but do not separate the remaining items.
- table: kim_2023_phq9
  issue: |-
    The PHQ-9 was administered in Korean (the Lee et al. 2014 Korean adaptation), but no Korean
    wording is published in the paper or its SPSS deposit, so the item and option text here is the
    instrument publisher's official English (phqscreeners.com) rather than the sentences respondents
    read. The shipped instruction is the PHQ-9's own 'Over the last 2 weeks', while the paper's
    Methods describes its PHQ-9 as asking about depression experiences over the past two months. The
    deposit's columns are unlabelled, so codes are tied to wording by the form's printed numbering;
    data checks pin PHQ9_4 (fatigue), PHQ9_9 (self-harm) and the somatic/cognitive split but do not
    separate the remaining items.
- table: kim_2025_isi
  issue: |-
    The Insomnia Severity Index was administered in Korean, but no Korean wording exists in the
    deposit or the paper, so the text is English from two different sources: the seven item stems
    are the published English ISI wording from Lenderking et al. (2024), not a translation of what
    these respondents read, while the option anchors are the study's own English labels from its S1
    File. Response codes run 1-5, not the ISI's published 0-4, so a total summed from the raw resp
    values is inflated by 7 relative to the standard 0-28 ISI total. Item 4's anchors as the study
    labelled them run 'completely unaware' to 'fully aware' rather than the standard form's 'not at
    all noticeable' to 'very much noticeable'. No source ties a code to a stem; the mapping is
    reconstructed from the S1 File's per-column value labels and same-file cross-checks.
- table: kim_2025_psas
  issue: |-
    The Korean Pre-Sleep Arousal Scale was administered in Korean, but no Korean wording appears in
    the paper or its single supplementary file, so the item text here is the English wording the
    authors print in their Table 3 rather than the sentences respondents read. The response labels
    are the deposit's own legend (1 = not at all ... 5 = very often), which differs from the paper's
    Methods sentence describing the scale as running from 1 (not at all) to 5 (extremely).
- table: kokoszka_2022_hamd
  issue: |-
    Item text is a canonical public-domain English reproduction of Hamilton's HDRS-17, not the
    wording used here: the scale was rated in Polish by psychiatrists following the SIGH-D
    interview guide, and the deposit (a bare CSV of integers) publishes no Polish wording. Codes
    are matched to the instrument's own numbering. ham16a and ham16b are the HDRS's two alternate
    ratings of the single item 16 (weight loss by patient report vs by weekly measurement), not
    two items; both are scored for every patient, but only ham16b enters the paper's HAM-D total.
- table: komura_2026_gqs_animacy
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The block is a
    5-item variant of Godspeed Animacy, not the canonical 6-item subscale -- 'Inactive <-> Active'
    and 'Sleepy <-> Awake' are not canonical Animacy pairs -- so the wording is this study's own,
    and no published Godspeed wording was substituted.
- table: komura_2026_gqs_anthropomorphism
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The anchors
    are also an adaptation rather than the canonical Godspeed Anthropomorphism set: items 4 and 5
    (Still-Lively, Mechanical-Organic) are Godspeed animacy anchors, and the canonical Fake-Natural
    and Moving rigidly-Moving elegantly pairs were not used. The study's wording is shipped as
    given, not normalised to the published instrument.
- table: komura_2026_gqs_likeability
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. That
    translation departs from the published Godspeed Likeability subscale, and is shipped as given:
    items 1 and 3 carry the identical text "Unpleasant <-> Pleasant" (most likely two distinct
    Japanese pairs rendered into one English phrase, so the two cannot be told apart), and item 5
    is "Scary <-> Not scary", which belongs to no Godspeed subscale. Only item 5 is pinned to its
    code by the data; the order of items 1-4 rests on the S2 File's numbering.
- table: komura_2026_gqs_perceived_intelligence
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The block
    departs from the published Godspeed Perceived Intelligence subscale: the canonical fifth pair
    "Foolish - Sensible" is replaced by "Unresponsive <-> Responsive", a Godspeed animacy anchor
    the study also administered as Animacy item 4. Items 1, 3 and 5 (Competent, Knowledgeable,
    Intelligent) are not separated by the data, so their order rests on the S2 File's numbering.
- table: komura_2026_gqs_perceived_safety
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. It departs
    slightly from the published Godspeed Perceived Safety subscale, shipped as given: "Calm" where
    the canonical set has "Relaxed", "Peaceful" where it has "Quiescent", and item 2 printed as
    "Calm - Agitated", so "Calm" is the high pole of item 1 and the low pole of item 2. Responses
    are stored raw: items 2 and 3 are reverse-keyed and must be reversed before scoring.
- table: komura_2026_mdmt_capable
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The paper
    cites Lee & See's trust-in-automation work, but the items are verbatim the Capable subscale of
    Ullman & Malle's Multi-Dimensional Measure of Trust. Only item 4 (Meticulous) is pinned to its
    code by the data; items 1-3 rest on the S2 File's numbering.
- table: komura_2026_mdmt_ethical
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The wording
    is the study's rather than the canonical MDMT Ethical subscale ('Has integrity' is third and
    'Honest/upright' fourth). The four near-synonymous adjectives share one 0-7 scale and the
    paper publishes no per-item statistics, so their assignment to mdmt_ethical_1..4 follows the
    S2 File's numbering and is not confirmed against the data.
- table: komura_2026_mdmt_reliable
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. It departs
    from the published MDMT Reliable subscale at one position, shipped as given: item 3 is
    "Dependable" where the canonical subscale reads "someone you can count on". The data do not
    separate item 1 from item 3 or item 2 from item 4, so order within the block rests on the S2
    File's numbering.
- table: komura_2026_mdmt_sincere
  issue: |-
    Respondents answered in Japanese; the item text is the authors' own English translation from
    their S2 File, because no Japanese wording is published anywhere in the deposit. The four
    sincerity words are near-synonyms and the paper reports no per-item statistics, so their order
    within the block rests on the S2 File's numbering alone.
- table: kuczyk_2024_facemask_fba
  issue: |-
    Item text is the authors' own English rendering from the variable labels of their SPSS file;
    the questionnaire was administered in German and no German wording is published in the deposit
    or supplements. The response anchors are the .sav's value labels, which differ in wording from
    the paper's Methods gloss (1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree); both are the
    authors' English for the same German scale.
- table: kuczyk_2024_facemask_fbe
  issue: |-
    Item text is the authors' own English rendering from the variable labels of their SPSS file;
    the questionnaire was administered in German and no German wording is published in the deposit
    or supplements (the authors say the questionnaires are available on request). The response
    anchors are the .sav's value labels (1 = definitely disagree ... 5 = definitely agree), which
    the paper's Methods renders instead as 1 = strongly disagree ... 5 = strongly agree.
- table: kuehner_2017_mw_rumination
  issue: |-
    The two probes were administered in German to students in Mannheim, but no German wording is
    published in the paper or any of its supplementary files, so the item text is the authors'
    own English from the paper's Methods rather than the sentences respondents read.
- table: laksmita_2020_mspss
  issue: |-
    The study administered an Indonesian translation of the MSPSS, but neither the paper nor its
    S1 Dataset publishes the Indonesian wording, so the canonical English MSPSS is shipped in its
    place, including the canonical form's instructions and its anchors for points 2-6 (the paper
    states only the 1 and 7 endpoints). Where the paper's own English differs from the canonical
    form (item 2, 'share my joys and sorrows'), the canonical wording is shipped.
- table: latifi_2026_insect_fear
  issue: |-
    The wording is the study's own English questionnaire (S1 Table); the children answered a
    Persian version the article does not publish. The response scale shipped for Q1-Q23 runs
    1 = Strongly agree to 5 = Strongly disagree, the OPPOSITE of the direction in both the SPSS
    deposit's value labels and the Methods section; the data force it -- only this direction
    reproduces the paper's published age correlations. Q24-Q32 run 1 = Never to 5 = Always.
- table: li_2021_cultural_intelligence
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered to employees of Chinese enterprises, but the deposit
    publishes only an English version (S1 Appendix contains no Chinese text), so the item text is
    the authors' own English rather than what respondents read. The administration language is
    inferred from the sample and survey platform; the paper does not state it. The data confirm
    which facet each item belongs to but not the order within a facet, which rests on the S1
    Appendix numbering.
- table: li_2021_knowledge_sharing
  issue: |-
    The survey was fielded to employees of Chinese enterprises and was in all likelihood
    administered in Chinese (the paper does not state the language), but the only questionnaire
    published is in English, so the item text is the authors' own English rendering rather than
    the wording respondents read. The data do not separate KS2 from KS4, so their order rests on
    the S1 Appendix numbering.
- table: li_2021_sustainable_innov_behav
  issue: |-
    The survey was fielded to employees of 31 Chinese enterprises and was in all likelihood
    administered in Chinese (the paper does not state the language), but the only questionnaire
    published is in English, so the item text is the authors' own English rendering rather than
    the wording respondents read. The data do not order SIB4 against SIB5 or SIB1 against SIB3,
    so those rest on the S1 Appendix numbering; SIB4 and SIB5 are the two items the paper dropped
    from its analysis.
- table: li_2024_bdyz
  issue: |-
    Despite the dictionary's 'body-image' description, this is the ERQ expressive-suppression
    subscale. Item text is the ERQ's original English; the study administered the scale in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published in the deposit or its supplements. The deposit numbers its
    four columns 1, 2, 6, 9 while the ERQ numbers its suppression items 2, 4, 6, 9, so bdyz_1
    carries ERQ item 4 ("When I am feeling positive emotions, I am careful not to express them")
    by elimination rather than a stated correspondence.
- table: liang_2026_intrinsic_motivation
  issue: |-
    The questionnaire was administered in Chinese and only the authors' English is published, so
    English is what ships. The paper never prints the IM1-IM5 codes; the assignment follows Table
    1's order and is confirmed item by item against the per-item means and SDs in Table 8. The
    paper prints item 2 two ways (Table 1: "I would use the app to learn more about sports if time
    permits"; Table 8: "If time permits, I would use ..."); the Table 1 form ships.
- table: lys_2020_rape_3_diff
  issue: |-
    Administered in Polish; the item text is the study's own English rendering from its SPSS
    labels, since the Polish originals are in neither the deposit nor the paper. The 13 items are
    not one scale: they form two opposed subscales, belief in biological and in social origins of
    gender differences, which the deposit scores separately. Do not sum all 13.
- table: lys_2020_rape_3_rwa
  issue: |-
    The Polish in `item_text` is NOT established as what respondents read: it comes from
    Radkiewicz (2011), an Altemeyer/Duckitt-lineage 20-item Polish RWA, whereas the study cites
    Grzesiak-Feldman's (2012) Polish adaptation of Funke's 12-item scale. The twelve items match in
    content, one appendix item each, but the Polish strings may differ. For this table the study's
    own English in `item_text_translated` is the more authoritative record. The six odd-coded
    reverse-worded items are already recoded in the deposit; do not reverse them again.
- table: lys_2020_rape_3_sj
  issue: |-
    Administered in Polish; the item text is the study's own English rendering from its SPSS
    labels, since the Polish originals are in neither the deposit nor the paper. sj3 and sj7 are
    reverse-worded but already recoded in the deposit, so higher resp means more system
    justification for every item; do not reverse them again.
- table: lys_2020_rape_3_unjust
  issue: |-
    Administered in Polish; the item text is the study's own English rendering from its SPSS
    labels, since the Polish originals are in neither the deposit nor the paper.
- table: moe2025_scs
  issue: |-
    The scale was administered to Italian teachers, but the deposit is an SPSS file with no item
    wording in any language. The Italian in `item_text` is the published Italian Self-Compassion
    Scale from the instrument's own site (self-compassion.org), and the English in the
    `_translated` columns is Neff's original SCS-26, so neither comes from the study's own
    materials. Codes are matched to the instrument's printed item numbers.
- table: odachi_2022_fear_covid19
  issue: |-
    The Japanese item text is the published Japanese FCV-19S (Wakashima et al. 2020), matched by
    item number, rather than wording supplied by this study. The English item and option wording
    in the `_translated` columns is the originators' own (Ahorsu et al. 2020), but the English
    instruction line was written by IRW, because neither source publishes one.
- table: orovou_2021_lec5
  issue: |-
    The study administered its own Greek translation of the LEC-5 and never published it; the
    English shipped is the wording in the study's SPSS file, verbatim the National Center for
    PTSD's LEC-5 Standard form. The response options are the study's recoding, not the
    instrument's: the LEC-5's six exposure categories are collapsed to 0 = No and 1 = It happened
    to me/I was a witness, and no instructions are given because the published ones describe a
    format these respondents did not see.
- table: orovou_2021_pcl5
  issue: |-
    The study administered a Greek translation of the PCL-5 but published no Greek wording, so the
    item text is the National Center for PTSD's English original (verbatim against the standard
    form) rather than what respondents read. The paper's Methods describes the scale as 1-5, while
    the deposit and the shipped anchors are the canonical 0-4 (0 = Not at all, 4 = Extremely).
    Instructions are blank because the reference window (past month vs past week) is not stated.
- table: ozkurt_2026_basic_psych_needs
  issue: |-
    The study administered a Turkish adaptation of the Basic Needs Satisfaction in Sport Scale and
    published no Turkish wording; the English here is the authors' own rendering from their S6
    File, which pairs one-for-one and in order with the 14 items of the original BNSSS (Ng,
    Lonsdale & Hodge, 2011) but diverges slightly from its wording (e.g. 'I show interest in my
    teammates' vs 'I show concern for others in my sport'). Despite the dictionary description,
    this is the BNSSS, not Deci & Ryan's Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction Scale.
- table: ozkurt_2026_ego_orientation
  issue: |-
    Despite the table name, this is the complete 10-item goal orientation questionnaire: EGOQ1, 3,
    4, 6 and 9 measure task orientation, not ego orientation. The study administered a Turkish
    adaptation (Ersoz et al., 2017) and published no Turkish wording; the English is the authors'
    own rendering from their S6 File, which pairs in order with the original GOEM (Petherick &
    Markland, 2008) but recasts every item as a self-contained 'I feel good when...' sentence in
    place of the GOEM's shared stem.
- table: pakseresht_2021_gmfood_risk_ranking
  issue: |-
    The English is the authors' own translation of a Swedish administration; the Swedish original
    is not in the article or any supplement. Respondents ranked the four risk dimensions after
    reading one of four randomly assigned GM-policy scenarios (Banned, R&D, Import, Full); that
    scenario text is not recorded in the response table, so the instructions carry a
    '<<[policy scenario]>>' placeholder where each respondent saw a different description.
- table: pang_2023_behavioral_intent
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_media_influence
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_perceived_cost
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_perceived_ease_use
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_perceived_enjoyment
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_perceived_risk
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement, i.e. less perceived risk.
- table: pang_2023_perceived_usefulness
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: pang_2023_social_norms
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English rendering; the questionnaire was administered in Chinese
    and no Chinese wording is published (the S2 File, despite its title, is English only). The
    paper's Methods states 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, but the shipped anchors run
    the other way (1 = Definitely agree ... 5 = Definitely disagree), following the questionnaire's
    display order, which the deposit's demographic codes corroborate -- higher resp means MORE
    disagreement.
- table: park_2024_ageism
  issue: |-
    Item text is the study's own English questionnaire (S2 File); the scale was administered in
    Korean to Korean clinical nurses and no Korean wording is published. Responses are stored raw,
    so the four pro-elderly items (a4, a6, a11, a12) run opposite to the other fourteen; reverse
    them before scoring. The paper's Methods describes the 29-item Fraboni Scale of Ageism, but the
    questionnaire and the deposit both hold 18 items, and the paper's Table 2 statistics do not
    reproduce from the deposit.
- table: pauli_2021_coercion_attitudes
  issue: |-
    The study administered a German ad hoc translation of the Staff Attitude to Coercion Scale,
    which was never deposited, so the English wording from the study's own codebook ships
    instead. The paper's Methods describes a 1-6 scale running from agreement to disagreement,
    while the deposited responses are 0-5 with 5 = fully agree; the shipped anchors follow the
    deposit.
- table: pavic_2022_healthcare_trust
  issue: |-
    The item text here is English, but the study was administered in Croatian to 577 college-
    and university-educated respondents in Croatia, and neither the paper nor its supplements
    publishes the Croatian wording, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English
    is the study's own, taken from the variable labels in its SPSS deposit, and matches 8 of the 9
    items of Shea et al.'s (2008) revised Health Care System Distrust Scale word for word (Shea's
    item 7, on equal treatment regardless of race or ethnicity, was dropped by the authors).
    Responses are stored raw: HCS_trust2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are reverse-worded and must be reversed
    before a trust total is scored.
- table: pavic_2022_natural_immunity
  issue: |-
    The item text here is English, but the study was administered in Croatian to 577 college-
    and university-educated respondents in Croatia (the instruments were translated and
    back-translated), and neither the paper nor its supplements publishes the Croatian wording,
    so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English is the study's own, taken from
    the variable labels in its SPSS deposit, and matches the three natural-immunity items of
    Martin & Petrie's (2017) published VAX scale verbatim.
- table: pavic_2022_science_literacy
  issue: |-
    The item text here is English, but the study was administered in Croatian to 577 college-
    and university-educated respondents in Croatia, and neither the paper nor its supplements
    publishes the Croatian wording, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English
    is the study's own, taken from the variable labels in its SPSS deposit, and matches the 15
    statements in the paper's Table 4. The response levels are the study's scoring, not the
    options respondents chose from: participants marked each statement true, untrue or don't
    know, and the deposit keeps only the dichotomised result, so resp 0 pools incorrect and
    don't-know answers. Table 4's 72.77% correct for the genetically-modified-fruit item (Lit6)
    is not attainable over 577 respondents; the data give 72.27% (417 of 577).
- table: pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy
  issue: |-
    The item text here is English, but the study was administered in Croatian to 577 college-
    and university-educated respondents in Croatia (the instruments were translated and
    back-translated), and neither the paper nor its supplements publishes the Croatian wording,
    so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English is the study's own, taken from
    the variable labels in its SPSS deposit, and matches the seven stems of Shapiro et al.'s
    Vaccine Conspiracy Beliefs Scale as the paper prints them in Table 1.
- table: pellerin2020_cpc_hope
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the CPC-12's published English (Lorenz et al., 2016, S1 Appendix), but
    the study was run in France and administered the scale in French; no French wording appears
    in the OSF deposit or the article, so the English stands in for what respondents read. Only
    the endpoint anchors (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree) are published, as the
    article's English gloss; points 2-6 are unlabelled. The deposit's columns carry no labels, so
    Hope_1..Hope_3 are matched to CPC-12 hope items 1-3 by instrument order.
- table: pellerin2020_cpc_optimism
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the CPC-12's published English (Lorenz et al., 2016, S1 Appendix), but
    the study was run in France and administered the scale in French; no French wording appears
    in the OSF deposit or the article, so the English stands in for what respondents read, and
    the 1 = strongly disagree / 7 = strongly agree anchors are likewise the article's English
    gloss. The mapping of Opt_1..Opt_3 onto CPC-12 items 4-6 is inferred from item order and only
    partly verified: Opt_1 is pinned by its age correlation (only item 4 mentions "the life ahead
    of me"), but Opt_2 and Opt_3 are near-synonymous and are separated only by an assumption
    about parent-scale cohesion.
- table: pellerin2020_cpc_selfefficacy
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the CPC-12's published English (Lorenz et al., 2016, S1 Appendix), but
    the study was run in France and administered the scale in French; no French wording appears
    in the OSF deposit or the article, so the English stands in for what respondents read, and
    the 1 = strongly disagree / 7 = strongly agree anchors are likewise the article's English
    gloss. The mapping of SAE_1..SAE_3 onto CPC-12 items 10-12 is inferred from item order: age
    gradients, endorsement levels and well-being correlations all pick this assignment, but the
    items' intercorrelation ordering does not replicate the CPC-12's development samples, so it
    is not fully verified.
- table: pellerin2020_gq6
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the GQ-6's original published English (McCullough, Emmons & Tsang,
    2002, Appendix A), but the study administered the French GQ-6 of Shankland & Martin-Krumm
    (2012) to a French sample; no French wording appears in the OSF deposit or the article, so
    the English stands in for what respondents read. The article prints only the endpoints (1 =
    strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree); the five intermediate labels come from the GQ-6's
    published form, not from the study. GQ_1..GQ_6 are mapped to GQ-6 items 1-6 by order,
    verified only at block level: GQ_3 and GQ_6 are confirmed as the reverse-keyed pair, but
    nothing distinguishes GQ_1 from GQ_2 or GQ_4 from GQ_5.
- table: pierro_2018_assessment_s1
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the original English Regulatory Mode Questionnaire (Kruglanski et al.,
    2000), but Study 1 administered an Italian version to 323 Italian adults, and neither the
    PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian wording, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The three reverse-worded items (assR1, assR5, assR11) are stored
    already reverse-recoded, so their anchors are flipped: for these, resp 1 = Strongly Agree and
    resp 6 = Strongly Disagree with the printed statement. Only the endpoints of the 6-point
    scale are labelled, following the paper's description of the administration.
- table: pierro_2018_assessment_s3
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the original English Regulatory Mode Questionnaire (Kruglanski et al.,
    2000), but Study 3 administered the same Italian version used in Study 1, and neither the
    PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian wording, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The deposit's columns carry no labels, so the wording is matched
    to the codes by the instrument's subscale order and the positions of the reverse-worded items
    (1, 5 and 11). Unlike Study 1, those three items (assr1, assr5, assr11) are stored raw here,
    not reverse-recoded.
- table: pierro_2018_locomotion_s1
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the original English Regulatory Mode Questionnaire (Kruglanski et al.,
    2000), but Study 1 administered an Italian version to 323 Italian adults, and neither the
    PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian wording, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The two reverse-worded items (locaR6, locaR9) are stored already
    reverse-recoded, so their anchors are flipped: for these, resp 1 = Strongly Agree and resp 6 =
    Strongly Disagree with the printed statement. Only the endpoints of the 6-point scale are
    labelled, following the paper's description of the administration.
- table: pierro_2018_locomotion_s3
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the original English Regulatory Mode Questionnaire (Kruglanski et al.,
    2000), but Study 3 administered the same Italian version used in Study 1 to 85 Italian
    participants, and neither the PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian
    wording, so these are not the sentences respondents read. Unlike the Study 1 table, the two
    reverse-worded items (locr6, locr9) are stored raw here, so a high response on them means the
    reverse-worded statement is true of the respondent and must be reversed before scoring. Only
    the endpoints of the 6-point scale are labelled, following the paper's description.
- table: pierro_2018_selfforgive_s1
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the English wording printed in the study's own PLOS ONE article (its
    rendering of a 4-item adaptation of Wohl et al.'s State Self-Forgiveness Scale), but the
    scale was administered in Italian to 323 Italian adults and neither the article nor its SPSS
    deposit publishes the Italian form, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The two
    reverse-worded items (sforgiveR1 'rejecting of myself', sforgiveR3 'dislike toward myself')
    are stored already reverse-recoded, so their anchors are flipped: for these, resp 1 =
    Completely and resp 4 = Not at all. Only the endpoints of the 4-point scale are labelled.
- table: pierro_2018_selfforgive_s2
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the English wording printed in the study's own PLOS ONE article (its
    rendering of a 4-item adaptation of Wohl et al.'s State Self-Forgiveness Scale), but the
    scale was administered in Italian to 97 Italian university students and neither the article
    nor its SPSS deposit publishes the Italian form, so these are not the sentences respondents
    read. The two reverse-worded items (SforgiveR1 'rejecting of myself', SforgiveR3 'dislike
    toward myself') are stored already reverse-recoded, so their anchors are flipped: for these,
    resp 1 = Completely and resp 4 = Not at all. Only the endpoints of the 4-point scale are
    labelled.
- table: pierro_2018_tf_future_s4
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the Temporal Focus Scale's original English (Shipp, Edwards & Lambert,
    2009), but Study 4 was run in Italian and neither the PLOS ONE article nor its SPSS deposit
    publishes the Italian form, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The deposit's
    columns carry no labels, and TFfuture1-4 are assigned to the four future items in the
    instrument's published order; the data cannot confirm this, since the composite reproduces
    the paper's statistics under any reordering. Only resp 7 (Constantly) is labelled; the
    paper's other endpoint, 1 = Never, is absent because no respondent used it.
- table: pierro_2018_tf_past_s4
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the Temporal Focus Scale's original English (Shipp, Edwards & Lambert,
    2009), but Study 4 was run with Italian students and neither the PLOS ONE article nor its
    SPSS deposit publishes the Italian form, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The
    deposit's columns carry no labels, and TFpast1-4 are assigned to the four past items in the
    instrument's own order; the items are same-polarity near-synonyms, so a permutation would be
    undetectable. Treat the subscale as reliable and each sentence's attachment to a code as
    provisional.
- table: pilch_2021_coping_behavior
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English for their coping-behaviour scale (from the
    paper's S1 Table), but the survey was administered in Polish to Polish adults and no Polish
    wording appears in the deposit or supplements, so these are not the sentences respondents
    read. The deposit's variable labels give each code's subscale but no wording, so within each
    of the three subscales the statements are matched to codes by S1 Table's listing order; the
    data confirm subscale membership only, not the order inside a subscale.
- table: pilch_2021_fear_covid19
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the administered Polish Fear of COVID-19 Scale, taken from the Polish
    validation paper the study cites (Pilch, Kurasz & Turska-Kawa, 2021, Table 1). The English in
    the `_translated` columns is Ahorsu et al.'s original FCV-19S wording as that paper prints it,
    a parallel original rather than a translation of the Polish beside it. The Polish response
    anchors are not published, so option_text is blank and only the English endpoint labels (1 =
    strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) are carried in the `_translated` column.
- table: pilch_2021_fcv19s_validation
  issue: |-
    The item text is the Polish Fear of COVID-19 Scale as printed in the study's own deposited
    questionnaire (the Materials sheet of the PeerJ supplement). Ahorsu et al.'s original English
    wording is in the `_translated` columns. For items 5-7 the deposited Polish differs from the
    translation printed in the paper's Table 1: item 5 omits "w mediach społecznościowych" (on
    social media), and items 6 and 7 are phrased differently. The deposited version is shipped as
    the one respondents saw.
- table: pilch_2021_personality_ipip20
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the published Polish IPIP-BFM-20 form (Topolewska et al., 2014), not
    wording printed by this study, whose data file labels its columns only IPIP1-IPIP20. The
    English item statements are IPIP's own wording for the same numbered items, a parallel
    original rather than a translation of the Polish, while the English of the instructions and
    the five response anchors was written by IRW. The instructions are the paper-and-pencil
    form's ("mark an X in the box"), although this study ran online. Codes are matched to
    wording by the form's item numbering; the data confirm each item's trait and keying, but a
    swap between the two same-trait, same-direction items in a pair (e.g. IPIP1/IPIP11) would be
    invisible.
- table: pilch_2021_protection_motivation
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English for their protection-motivation questionnaire
    (from the paper's Table 1), but the survey was administered in Polish and no Polish wording
    appears in the deposit or supplements, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The
    deposit's variable labels give each code's subscale but no wording; within each two-item
    subscale, which statement is item 1 and which is item 2 follows Table 1's listing order and
    is not independently verified.
- table: powell_2018_qcae
  issue: |-
    The item wording is not from Powell's own materials: the deposit states only that each column
    is a QCAE item number, so the text is the canonical QCAE keyed by that number, taken from an
    independent QCAE deposit (Gomez et al., 2022) for 27 items and from the published instrument
    for the four reverse-worded items 1, 2, 17 and 29. The two middle anchors are the canonical
    QCAE labels; the study publishes only the endpoints. The data confirm subscale membership
    exactly, but order within a subscale rests on the item numbering. Responses are stored raw,
    so items 1, 2, 17 and 29 must be reversed before scoring.
- table: ptacek2023_dass21
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the Vilimovsky & Kucera Czech DASS-21 that the study names as its
    administered version, taken from the instrument's distribution site because neither the OSF
    deposit nor the paper reproduces it. The English in the `_translated` columns is the
    publisher's parallel English DASS-21, not a translation of the Czech, so some items do not
    correspond word for word (Czech item 8 reads "I felt that I was tense and nervous" where the
    English reads "I felt that I was using a lot of nervous energy"). The data confirm the
    depression/anxiety/stress partition, but order within a subscale rests on the code numbering.
- table: qi_2025_dark_triad
  issue: |-
    Respondents completed the Chinese Short Dark Triad (SD3-C; Zhang, Ziegler & Paulhus, 2020),
    but its wording appears in neither the OSF deposit nor the supplement, so the item text is
    the SD3's English original as distributed by its author (SD3.1.1) -- a parallel version of
    the same numbered items, not what respondents read. The 1-5 anchors are the English
    instrument's; the paper labels only the endpoints. Codes follow the SD3's item order, which
    the published subscale alphas confirm at block level but not within a block. Responses are
    stored raw: DT_11, DT_15, DT_17, DT_20 and DT_25 are reverse-keyed and not yet reversed.
- table: qi_2025_self_concept_clarity
  issue: |-
    The Self-Concept Clarity Scale was administered in Chinese, but its wording appears in
    neither the OSF deposit nor the supplement, so the item text is Campbell et al.'s (1996)
    English original -- a parallel version of the same numbered items, not what respondents
    read. Only the instrument's endpoints are labelled ('strongly disagree', 'strongly agree');
    the paper glosses them as 'very much disagree' / 'very much agree'. The deposit's scoring
    formula confirms which items are reverse-keyed, but order within the reverse block, and
    SCC_6 versus SCC_11, rest on the instrument's numbering. Responses are stored raw: the ten
    reverse-keyed items (all but SCC_6 and SCC_11) are not yet reversed.
- table: qi_2025_self_construal
  issue: |-
    The Self-Construal Scale was administered to Chinese university students, but no Chinese
    wording is published in the OSF deposit or the paper, so the item text is Singelis's English
    original, a parallel version rather than what respondents read. The study's own anchors (1 =
    very much disagree, 7 = very much agree) are used; the intermediate points are unlabelled.
    The deposit's scoring formulas confirm which items form the independent and interdependent
    subscales, and they match the published scale item for item.
- table: qi_2025_self_esteem
  issue: |-
    The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale was administered in Chinese, but no Chinese wording is
    published in the OSF deposit or supplement, so the item text is the RSES English original
    (University of Maryland form), not what respondents read. The study prints no item list and
    the RSES circulates in two orderings; the one shipped (reverse-worded items at Esteem_3, 5, 8,
    9 and 10) reproduces the paper's alpha of .89 where the other does not, but order within each
    polarity class is not pinned. Responses are stored raw and run 1 = strongly disagree to 4 =
    strongly agree as the paper states -- the reverse of the numbering on the instrument's own
    form, whose anchor words are used here.
- table: qi_2025_swls
  issue: |-
    The Satisfaction with Life Scale was administered to Chinese university students, but no
    Chinese wording is published in the OSF deposit or the paper, so the item text is Diener's
    English original, not what respondents read. SWLS_1-5 are assumed to be the published items
    1-5 in order; the deposit confirms which columns form the scale but not which item each code
    is. The anchors are the study's own (1 = completely disagree, 7 = completely agree), not the
    original's 'strongly disagree' / 'strongly agree'.
- table: qiang_2025_abusive_supervision
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the column headers of the study's S1
    File, but the questionnaire was translated into Chinese and administered to Chinese retail
    staff, and no Chinese wording for these items is published, so these are not the sentences
    respondents read. The paper never names or analyses this four-item block (questionnaire
    items 38-41), so the instrument name is IRW's description; the items resemble four of
    Tepper's (2000) abusive-supervision items but are reworded. Only the endpoints of the 1-5
    scale are labelled.
- table: qiang_2025_coping
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the column headers of the study's S1
    File, but the questionnaire was translated into Chinese and administered to 396 Chinese
    retail staff, and no Chinese wording for these items is published, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The paper never names or analyses this three-item block
    (questionnaire items 30-32); the label "coping" was assigned by IRW from item content, not
    by the authors. Only the endpoints of the 1-5 scale are labelled.
- table: qiang_2025_job_dissatisfaction
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the column headers of the study's S1
    File, but the questionnaire was translated into Chinese and administered to Chinese retail
    staff, and no Chinese wording for these five items is published, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. Only the endpoints of the 1-5 scale are labelled.
- table: qiang_2025_job_performance
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the column headers of the study's S1
    File, but the questionnaire was translated into Chinese and administered to Chinese retail
    staff, and no Chinese wording for these items is published, so these are not the sentences
    respondents read. The paper does not analyse or cite a source for this block (questionnaire
    items 17-21), so the instrument name is IRW's description. Only the endpoints of the 1-5
    scale are labelled.
- table: qin_2025_behavioral_intention
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the paper's S1 Table, but the 547
    respondents were domestic Chinese tourists answering a Chinese-language questionnaire, and no
    Chinese wording is published in the article or its supplements, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The source never states the 1-6 scale's anchors, so option_text
    is blank.
- table: qin_2025_perceived_cultural_distance
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the paper's S1 Table, but the 547
    respondents were domestic Chinese tourists answering a Chinese-language questionnaire, and no
    Chinese wording is published in the article or its supplements, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The source never states the 1-6 scale's anchors, so option_text
    is blank.
- table: qin_2025_tourism_experience
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the paper's S1 Table, but the 547
    respondents were domestic Chinese tourists answering a Chinese-language questionnaire, and no
    Chinese wording is published in the article or its supplements, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The source never states the 1-6 scale's anchors, so option_text
    is blank. RCTE4 and RCTE5 keep the source's duplicated "gain a gain a" as printed.
- table: qin_2025_tourist_satisfaction
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the authors' own English from the paper's S1 Table, but the 547
    respondents were domestic Chinese tourists answering a Chinese-language questionnaire, and no
    Chinese wording is published in the article or its supplements, so these are not the
    sentences respondents read. The source never states the 1-6 scale's anchors, so option_text
    is blank.
- table: reinecke_2018_online_vigilance
  issue: |-
    The Online Vigilance Scale was administered in German, but neither the article nor its
    Supporting Information datasets publish any German wording, so the item text and the two
    endpoint anchors here are the English of the study's own SPSS variable and value labels, not
    the sentences respondents read. Scale points 2-4 carry no option text.
- table: reinwarth_2023_domain_importance
  issue: |-
    The German item and option text is the FLZM questionnaire as respondents saw it, taken from a
    published reproduction of the instrument rather than the study's terse data labels. The
    English in the `_translated` columns is Schwinn et al.'s (2026) printed translation, and its
    label for resp 2, 'rather not important', is a loose rendering of the administered German
    'Etwas wichtig' (somewhat important).
- table: reyes_2022_eheals
  issue: |-
    The study's survey and data file do not reproduce the eHEALS wording -- both point to Table 1
    of Norman & Skinner (2006) -- so the item text and instructions are the published
    instrument's. The instructions keep the interviewer phrasing "tell me which response best
    reflects your opinion" although this study fielded the scale online. The response anchors
    follow the study's own data key, 1 = Strongly agree to 5 = Strongly disagree, which is the
    reverse of the instrument's own coding, and the midpoint reads 'Neither agree nor disagree'
    where the instrument prints 'Undecided'.
- table: rfq_wozniakprus_2021
  issue: |-
    The RFQ-8 was administered in Polish, but neither the deposit nor the closed-access paper
    contains Polish item wording and the rights holder's official Polish form is no longer
    distributed, so the item text is the canonical English RFQ-8, not what respondents read. All
    eight items run 1 = Strongly disagree to 7 = Strongly agree; the source file labels RFQ8 in the
    opposite direction, which is an error in the source and is overridden here. In IRW versions
    before the 2026-09 correction, RFQ8's response values 1 and 7 were swapped (88 of 538
    responses); results that scored RFQ8 from those versions should be rerun.
- table: teq_novak_2021_scbs
  issue: |-
    The Santa Clara Brief Compassion Scale was administered in Czech, but the Czech wording is not
    published, so the item text is English, not what respondents read. SCBCS_1-5 are assumed to
    follow the published item order; nothing in the deposit states it and the data cannot
    separate item 2 from item 3. The English is transcribed from a source that ends item 1 at
    "compassion" (other printings add "for him or her") and prints item 5 with the typo "when the
    seem to be in need". The anchors are this study's 7-point ones (1 = Not at all true of me, 7
    = Very true of me), not the source's 5-point format.
- table: teq_novak_2021_spirit
  issue: |-
    The Daily Spiritual Experience Scale was administered in a 15-item Czech version whose wording
    is not published, so the item text is Underwood's English original, not what respondents
    read; the Czech form drops Underwood's item 5, and codes are matched through the published
    renumbering. Direction: 1 = Many times a day and 6 = Never or almost never, so a higher value
    means less frequent spiritual experience -- the paper's statement that a higher score means
    more spirituality contradicts its own anchors, and the data follow the anchors. SPIRIT_15 (the
    closeness-to-God item) is on four points running the same way, 1 closest, reversed relative to
    Underwood's printed order. Misspelt codes such as SIPRIT_8 and SPRIT_14 are source typos kept
    as join keys.
- table: VSOCFP_Sebo_2024
  issue: |-
    The item text here is the administered French SOC-13/SOC-8 wording from the study's Multimedia
    Appendix 1. The English in the `_translated` columns is not the study's own: the item wording is
    quoted from a published English SOC-13 item table (Islam et al. 2025) and the 1/7 anchors from a
    different published source (Bonanato et al. 2022), so it is a parallel English version rather
    than a translation of the French, and the English instructions were translated from the French
    by IRW.
- table: Veterans_Affairs_SSVF_Survey_2016-17
  issue: |-
    Item 58's wording is taken from the 2015 form ('since you finished receiving services'), because
    the FY2016-2017 wording is not published; the neighbouring items 56 and 57 were reworded to
    'since you started' by the FY2018-2020 form, so what FY2016-2017 respondents read for item 58
    may differ. Item 7 ('Q8 into', stored value always 1) carries no text, and items 43, 49 and 55
    -- the write-in sixth 'Other Supportive Services' row -- carry only the block stem with no
    service label. Item 3 runs 1 = Very Dissatisfied to 5 = Very Satisfied, confirmed against the
    published year-end totals and its +0.87 correlation with item 1; this is the reverse of the
    direction the VA data dictionary states for the FY2018-2020 satisfaction items.
- table: abdullah_2024_hpbbloat_stress
  issue: |-
    The source publishes wording only for the final, renumbered 17-item form, which interleaves the
    five subscales, and the deposited data carry the original SM codes with no labels. Which
    statement each stress-management code holds (SM1 -> item 4, SM2 -> 9, SM4 -> 13, SM8 -> 17) is
    therefore inferred by assuming the subscale's items kept their ascending order; no published
    source confirms it, so the four texts could be permuted among these codes.
- table: brand_raffaelli_2024_familiarity_24
  issue: |-
    The numbered item codes are question positions in a counterbalanced design, not brands: each
    respondent was randomised to one of ten brand lists, so each code was answered about ten
    different brands, and the list assignment is not carried in the IRW table -- items cannot be
    tied to a brand. The item text uses the brand-name survey's wording; rows with item_family =
    logo were rated on a logo image and their prompt read 'this logo' rather than 'this brand'.
- table: brand_raffaelli_2024_liking_20
  issue: |-
    The numbered item codes are question positions in a counterbalanced design, not brands: each
    respondent was randomised to one of ten brand lists, so each code was answered about ten
    different brands, and the list assignment is not carried in the IRW table -- items cannot be
    tied to a brand. The item text uses the brand wording; the two logo administrations read 'this
    logo'. In addition, the logo Familiarity-Liking subsample's responses (about 305 respondents)
    were mis-recoded during processing -- values shifted one point, with 'Dislike' stored as 7 -- so
    the 1 = Dislike / 7 = Like anchors shown do not describe those rows.
- table: brand_raffaelli_2024_liking_24
  issue: |-
    The numbered item codes are question positions in a counterbalanced design, not brands: each
    respondent was randomised to one of ten brand lists, so each code was answered about ten
    different brands, and the list assignment is not carried in the IRW table -- items cannot be
    tied to a brand. The item text uses the brand-name survey's wording; rows with item_family =
    logo were rated on a logo image and their prompt read 'like or dislike this logo'.
- table: content_literacy_intervention_g1
  issue: |-
    Only the 20 reading-motivation items (codes 1-20) carry text; the 96 science and social-studies
    vocabulary items (codes 21-116) are blank because no accessible source names their target words.
    The motivation wording is the Me and My Reading Profile adaptation printed in Appendix G of the
    project's preceding first-grade trial (ERIC ED662409), since this study's own copy of the form
